question: You may use your horn on narrow mountain roads
options: "a: To alert oncoming traffic where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead,b: To let pedestrians know you are there,c: To signal to other drivers that you are in a hurry"
note: "The DMV Handbook states on page 12: 'Use your vehicle's horn to let other drivers know you are there or warn others of a hazard. Use your horn to: Avoid collisions. Alert oncoming traffic on narrow mountain roads where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead.'"

question: You should signal continuously while turning because it:
options: "a: Is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b: Lets other drivers know what your intentions are.,c: Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn."
note: "The DMV handbook states that you should signal when you turn because 'Always signal when you turn, change lanes, slow down, or stop. You can signal using your vehicle's signal lights or using hand-and-arm positions.'"

question: When both right and left turn signals are flashing at the same time on a moving vehicle, it means
options: "a: It is carrying children to or from school,b: Let the vehicle have the right-of-way,c: There may be a hazard or an accident ahead"
note: "If you can see a collision or hazard ahead, warn drivers behind you using these methods: Turn on your emergency flashers. Lightly tap your brake pedal three or four times. Use a hand signal when slowing and stopping."

question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:
options: "a: Stay in the right lane as much as possible because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.,b: Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder so that you can pass.,c: Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass."
note: "To safely pass a motorcycle that is in the travel lane you may need to change to another lane. In this case, pass safely then return to your original lane. Leave space between your vehicle and the bicyclist."

question: Regulatory signs are
options: "a: Suggestions,b: Law,c: Warnings"
note: "On page 37, the DMV handbook states that 'Red and White Regulatory Sign Follow the sign's instruction.'"

question: It is illegal to leave a child age six or younger unattended in a vehicle on a hot day:
options: "a: Even if they are secured in a child passenger restraint system.,b: If they are supervised by a person twelve years of age or older.,c: Only if the key is in the ignition."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'It is illegal to leave a child who is six years old or younger unattended in a vehicle...' and 'A child may be left under the supervision of a person who is at least 12 years old.'"

question: A curb painted red means:
options: "a: Loading zone.,b: The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c: No parking"
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Red: No stopping, standing, or parking.'"

question: Left sign or the lane and sign should be used to warn of the reduction in the number of traffic lanes in the direction of travel on a multi lane highway. When parking uphill on a 2 way street with no curb, your front wheels should be
options: "a: Turn to the left toward the street,b: Turn to the right away from the street,c: Parallel with the pavement,d: Turn the wheels toward the curb"
note: "To prevent rolling downhill when parked on a hill with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right away from the street. 'Headed uphill: Turn your front wheels away from the curb (left - towards the center of the road) and let your vehicle roll back a few inches. The wheel should gently touch the curb. '"

question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:
options: "a: Buckle your safety belt.,b: Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c: Both of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook states that drivers should 'buckle up' and make sure that their 'passengers must wear seat belts.'"

question: You may make a left turn on a red light only from a:
options: "a: One-way street onto a two-way street.,b: One-way street onto a one-way street.,c: Two-way street onto a one-way street."
note: "You may turn left against a red light when you are turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists who have a green light. Look both ways and turn when it is safe."

question: If weather or light conditions require you to have your lights on while driving:
options: "a: Use your parking lights.,b: Use your high beams.,c: Use your low beams."
note: "According to page 11, 'Use your headlights: ...If you need to use your windshield wipers due to fog, rain, or snow, you must turn on your low-beam headlights.'"

question: If you pass a school bus that is stopped with its red lights flashing, you will:
options: "a: Be fined up to $1000,b: Be fined up to $100.,c: Face no legal consequences."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, on page 50, 'If you fail to stop, you may be fined up to $1,000 and your driving privilege could be suspended for one year.'"

question: What should a driver do when approaching a traffic control signal that is not in operation?
options: "a: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,b: If the intersection is clear,c: Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles."
note: "When a traffic light is not working, stop as if the intersection is controlled by STOP signs in all directions. Then proceed cautiously when it is safe to do so."

question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, drivers should:
options: "a: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c: Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'You may drive on or cross a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway or alley.'  This means drivers should stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area."

question: Dim your high beam headlights to low beams within
options: "a: 200 feet when a vehicle is coming towards you,b: 300 feet when a vehicle is coming towards you,c: 500 feet when a vehicle is coming towards you"
note: "According to The DMV handbook, 'Dim your high-beam headlights to low beams within 500 feet of a vehicle coming toward you or within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.' This information is found on page 11 of the DMV handbook."

question: When changing lanes on a freeway, you should:
options: "a: Signal for at least five seconds.,b: Slow down before you start to change lanes.,c: Assume there is enough space in the next lane for your vehicle"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Signal at least five seconds before you change lanes on a freeway.'"

question: Which of the following factors affect an individual's absorption of alcohol?
options: "a: Weight,b: Height,c: Intelligence"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Your BAC measures how much alcohol is present in your bloodstream.' It further provides a 'BLOOD ALCOHOL CONCENTRATION (BAC) Table' that includes different body weights to show how BAC is impacted.  This table shows that a person's weight is a factor that impacts alcohol absorption."

question: If you are driving and the rear end of your car starts skidding to the left, you should:
options: "a: Steer to the right.,b: Steer to the left.,c: Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral."
note: "To get out of a skid, you should steer in the direction of the skid. 'If you start to skid, follow these steps: 1. Slowly remove your foot from the accelerator. 2. Do not use the brakes. 3. Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid. 4. Try to get a wheel on dry pavement.'"

question: If you are the first person to stop to give assistance at a collision scene, you should drive to the side of the road
options: "a: After you have passed the collision scene,b: Before you reach the collision scene,c: Next to the collision scene"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 77: 'If you are in a collision, you must stop. Someone could be injured and need your help.'"

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: "a: Another name for a four-way intersection.,b: An area designated for road construction workers.,c: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway."
note: "A crosswalk is the part of the road set aside for pedestrians to safely cross the road. They are often marked with white lines. School crossings may have yellow crosswalk lines. Not all crosswalks are marked. Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks."

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
options: "a: Helps you stop faster.,b: Locks the front wheels of a vehicle,c: Keeps the brakes from freezing."
note: "The DMV handbook mentions that 'A locked wheel skid is usually caused by braking too hard when you are going too fast'."

question: What should a driver do who is stopped at an intersection and wants to make a left turn?
options: "a: Turn immediately if there are no pedestrians.,b: Take the right-of-way turn before oncoming traffic.,c: Give the right-of-way to any approaching vehicle that is close enough to be dangerous."
note: "When turning left, you must check for pedestrians. 'Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian or approaching vehicle that is close enough to be dangerous.'"

question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:
options: "a: To speed up slightly.,b: That it is not safe to pass.,c: To maintain a steady speed."
note: "The DMV handbook explains on page 37 that 'No Passing' signs indicate 'that it is not safe to pass'."

question: Dim your headlights for oncoming vehicles or when you are within 300 feet of a vehicle:
options: "a: That you are approaching from behind.,b: Approaching you from behind.,c: That you have already passed."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 11, 'Dim your high-beam headlights to low beams within 500 feet of a vehicle coming toward you or within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.'"

question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:
options: "a: Speed up slightly.,b: Prepare to stop,c: Maintain a steady speed."
note: "You should prepare to stop as you approach the top of a hill because you may not be able to see what is ahead.  The DMV handbook states: 'Do not pass if you are approaching a hill or curve and cannot see if other traffic is approaching. This is very dangerous on one and two lane roads.'"

question: You face a green light, but traffic on the other side of the intersection does not allow you to travel all the way through the intersection. What must you do?
options: "a: Wait for the next green light,b: Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection,c: Enter the intersection and wait until traffic ahead clears"
note: "It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.  'It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.'"

question: When driving in work zones, you should:
options: "a: Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b: Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 49, 'Go through the work zone carefully by: ... Allowing extra space between vehicles.'"

question: When entering the interstate, check for a gap in traffic in the nearest lane, adjust your speed to match traffic, signal, and:
options: "a: Expect traffic to allow you to proceed into the lane,b: Merge carefully into the gap.,c: Wait for the lane to clear before merging."
note: "The DMV handbook states that when entering a highway, you should 'Merge into highway traffic when safe to do so. Do not stop unless absolutely necessary.'"

question: It is more dangerous to drive at night than during the day because:
options: "a: You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b: The road is always more slippery at night.,c: Your reaction time is slower at night."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 59 that 'When driving at night, use your high-beam headlights on open country roads or dark city streets. Make sure you can stop in the distance lit by your headlights.'"

question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. You should:
options: "a: Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b: Merge across two lanes at once.,c: Always stop before entering the highway."
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'When you enter a highway, you will need to... Merge into highway traffic when safe to do so. Do not stop unless absolutely necessary.'"

question: Parallel parking is when the
options: "a: Front wheels are turned toward the street,b: Vehicle is in line with other parked vehicles,c: Rear wheels are touching the curb"
note: "Parallel parking is defined as parking 'in line with the road and other parked vehicles'.  The DMV handbook states that on page 26: 'Parallel parking is when you park in line with the road and other parked vehicles.'"

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to make a right turn, you should:
options: "a: Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b: Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.,c: Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb."
note: "The DMV handbook states that when turning right, you should drive close to the right edge of the road.  It also states that when turning right from a one-way street onto a one-way street, you should start the turn in the far-right lane.  This means you should wait for the truck or bus to turn before you turn, rather than quickly turning before them or squeezing between them and the curb."

question: You are passing a school and see children near the street. You may not drive faster than
note: "The DMV handbook states 'The speed limit is 25 mph within 500 feet of a school while children are outside or crossing the street.'"

question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: "a: Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b: Improve traffic flow.,c: Demonstrate defensive driving techniques."
note: "The DMV Handbook states, '...you should not block normal and reasonable traffic flow by driving too slowly.'  'If you drive faster or slower than the speed limit, you may be cited.' (Page 50)"

question: A person convicted of reckless driving or engaging in a speed contest that causes injury to another person is subject to
options: "a: imprisonment and a fine,b: community service,c: all the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'A person convicted of reckless driving or engaging in a speed contest that causes injury to another person is subject to imprisonment, a fine, or both.'"

question: You are driving on the freeway. The vehicle in front of you is a large truck. You should drive
options: "a: Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead,b: Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle to be out of the truck drivers blind spot,c: No more than one car length behind the truck,d: None of the above"
note: "Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle to be out of the truck drivers blind spot'. This is emphasized in the 'Blind Spots (The No Zone)' section of The DMV handbook on page 42: 'If you cannot see the truck's side mirrors, the truck driver cannot see you.'"

question: If a driver ahead of you has stopped at a crosswalk, you should
options: "a: Change lanes look carefully and pass,b: Tap your horn to let the driver know you are waiting,c: Stop then proceed when safe"
note: "You must stop for pedestrians at a crosswalk. 'Pedestrians always have the right-of-way. Here are some right-of-way rules at intersections:  - Green traffic signal light: Proceed with caution. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.'"

question: If your car goes into water, you should
options: "a: Wait for water to rush in and let it out in small breaths through your nose,b: Call the fire department immediately,c: Remove yourself before it starts to sink"
note: "The most important thing to do in this scenario is to get yourself out of the car before it sinks. 'It is important to understand the dangers of water on the road, including: Being swept off the road. Floating debris and unseen hazards. The road collapsing. Vehicle malfunction.'"

question: You may drive a motor vehicle in a bike lane:
options: "a: If you drive more slowly than 15 mph.,b: No more than 200 feet before making a right turn.,c: Whenever bicyclists are not present."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'It is illegal to drive in a bicycle lane unless you are: Parking (where permitted), Entering or leaving the road, Turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).'"

question: If you have a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, you should
options: "a: Enter the intersection and wait until traffic clears,b: Merge into another lane and try to go around the traffic,c: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears,d: None of the above"
note: "It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.  'It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.'"

question: When passing, you should move back into the right lane when:
options: "a: You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c: You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, you should move back into the right lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. 'Signal and return to your original lane.'"

question: Construction zone signs are generally:
options: "a: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,b: Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 37, 'Diamond-Shaped Sign' Warns you of specific road conditions and dangers ahead."

question: A curb painted blue means parking is:
options: "a: Allowed for no longer than 15 minutes.,b: Only allowed when picking up or dropping off passengers.,c: For disabled persons with a special placard or plate."
note: "According to page 28, 'Blue: Parking for a disabled person or someone driving a disabled person with a special placard or special license plate.'"

question: When you approach an octagonal sign, you must:
options: "a: Slow.,b: Stop.,c: Turn."
note: "An octagonal sign is a stop sign. 'Make a full stop before entering the crosswalk or at the limit line. If there is no limit line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Check traffic in all directions before proceeding.'"

question: Changing from one lane to another is best done:
options: "a: Quickly and often.,b: When a car is in your blind spot.,c: Gradually and carefully."
note: "Changing lanes should be done gradually and carefully to avoid collisions. 'Before you change lanes: … Be sure there is enough space for your vehicle in the next lane. It is not necessary to slow down before a lane change.'"

question: If you are facing a green traffic light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: "a: Turn left and find another route.,b: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c: Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection."
note: "Even if you have a green light, do not start across the intersection if there are pedestrians or vehicles blocking your pathway. It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red."

question: If you are feeling fatigued while driving, you should:
options: "a: Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.,b: Increase the volume of your radio.,c: Find a safe parking area to take a short nap."
note: "Fatigue and drowsiness can affect your vision and increase reaction time to hazards. 'Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.'  is the only option that directly addresses the issue of fatigue."

question: When entering the interstate, check for a gap in traffic in the nearest lane, adjust your speed to match traffic, signal, and:
options: "a: Expect traffic to allow you to proceed into the lane,b: Merge carefully into the gap.,c: Wait for the lane to clear before merging."
note: "The DMV handbook states that when entering a highway, you should 'Merge into highway traffic when safe to do so. Do not stop unless absolutely necessary.'"

question: Fines in a construction zone are:
options: "a: Doubled.,b: Tripled.,c: Cut in half."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 49, 'Fines are also doubled in highway construction or maintenance zones when workers are present.'"

question: Parking is never permitted
options: "a: In a crosshatched (diagonal) pattern space,b: In a bicycle lane unless otherwise posted,c: Twenty feet from a railroad track"
note: "According to page 28, 'Never park or leave your vehicle... In the crosshatched (diagonal lines) area next to a designated disabled parking space.'"

question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Yield the right-of-way to:
options: "a: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,b: All approaching vehicles.,c: Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a \"Walk\" signal."
note: "When turning left, check for pedestrians. Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian or approaching vehicle that is close enough to be dangerous."

question: You should signal at least 100 feet before you turn...
options: "a: Before every lane change.,b: At least 5 seconds before you change lanes on a freeway.,c: None of the above.,d: both a and b"
note: "The text states, 'You should signal: At least 100 feet before you turn, Before every lane change., At least five seconds before you change lanes on a freeway.'"

question: You see a signal person at a road construction site ahead. You should obey his or her instructions:
options: "a: Only if you see orange cones on the road ahead.,b: Unless they conflict with existing signs,c: At all times."
note: "On page 49, it is stated that 'Obey special signs or instructions from workers such as flaggers.'"

question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:
options: "a: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b: Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,c: Keep your wheels facing straight."
note: "As quoted in the DMV handbook: 'Headed either uphill or downhill when there is no curb: Turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail. Downhill: turn the wheels toward the curb.'"

question: Which of the following is not a safe driving practice when driving on the interstate?
options: "a: Slower traffic must keep to the right.,b: Change lanes without signaling.,c: If you miss your exit"
note: "The DMV handbook states 'Stay in one lane as much as possible. Do not weave in and out of traffic. Last minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.'  Changing lanes without signaling is not a safe driving practice, and it is not allowed on the interstate."

question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: "a: Often,b: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c: Never. It confuses other drivers."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Give up your right-of-way when it will help prevent collisions.'"

question: Which of the following increases your chances of being in a collision?
options: "a: Looking over your shoulder while making lane changes,b: Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles,c: Adjusting your rearview mirror before you start driving"
note: "Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles increases the risk of collision.  'Stay in one lane as much as possible. Do not weave in and out of traffic. Last minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.'"

question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:
options: "a: Buckle your safety belt.,b: Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c: Both of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook states that drivers should 'buckle up' and make sure that their 'passengers must wear seat belts.'"

question: Sleeping pills, tranquilizers, pain medicine, or cold or allergy medications
options: "a: May impair your driving,b: May increase the bad effects of alcohol on your driving,c: Both of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Prescription and over-the-counter medications can make you an unsafe driver.'  It also states that 'Some medicines can make you sleepy.'  Therefore, the answer is 'c', as the medications can impair driving and increase the negative effects of alcohol."

question: If traffic light is red, but a police officer or fire fighter on duty tells you to go ahead, you should
options: "a: Wait for the green light,b: Do as he or she tells you,c: Report him or her to police"
note: "Obey any direction, order, or signal given by a law enforcement officer, or firefighter. Follow their orders even if they conflict with existing signs, signals, or laws."

question: Looking down the road to where your vehicle will be in about 10 seconds helps you to
options: "a: enjoy the scenery,b: avoid last minute moves,c: see hazards inside your car"
note: "Scanning the road at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle helps you avoid last minute moves and hazards. 'To give yourself time to react, avoid last minute moves and hazards, always keep your eyes moving and scan the road at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.'"

question: With a Class C driver's license, a person may drive
options: "a: a light rail train,b: car or van or pickup truck,c: semi truck"
note: "On page 7, The DMV handbook states 'Most people need a noncommercial Class C driver's license.'  On page 1, it states 'For information on vehicles covered by a Class C, visit dmv.ca.gov/dl.'"

question: How many days do you have to report to DMV the sale or transfer of your vehicle?
options: "a: 5 days,b: 10 days,c: 20 days"
note: "According to page 79, 'When you sell a vehicle, you must notify DMV within five days by completing a Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability at dmv.ca.gov/nrl.'"

question: To prevent tailgating, drivers should follow the:
options: "a: One-second rule.,b: Two-second rule.,c: Three-second rule."
note: "To prevent tailgating, drivers should use the three-second rule to ensure a safe following distance and avoid a collision. 'Use the three-second rule to ensure a safe following distance and avoid a collision.' "

question: You should use your turn signals...
options: "a: When changing lanes or merging into traffic.,b: When turning left or right.,c: Both of the above.,d: None of the above"
note: "The DMV Handbook states that you should 'Always signal when you turn, change lanes, slow down, or stop.'  This includes both turning left or right and changing lanes or merging."

question: It is dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely because:
options: "a: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c: They brake more slowly than motor vehicles."
note: "According to page 44, 'Allow a safe three-second following distance. This space will help you avoid hitting a motorcyclist if they brake suddenly or fall.'"

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:
options: "a: Stop,b: Stop if you are driving in the same direction.,c: Slow down and be prepared to stop."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'All vehicles must stop for school buses. When the bus flashes red lights (located at the top, front, and back of the bus), you must stop from either direction until the children are safely across the street and the lights stop flashing. Remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.'"

question: If you have a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, you should
options: "a: Enter the intersection and wait until traffic clears,b: Merge into another lane and try to go around the traffic,c: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears,d: None of the above"
note: "It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red. question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should drive:
options: "a: Near the right-hand side of the road.,b: Near the centerline.,c: On the left of the centerline."
note: "To make a left turn, you should drive 'close to the center divider or into the left turn lane.'"

question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, drivers should:
options: "a: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c: Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'You may drive on or cross a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway or alley.'  This means drivers should stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area."

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane:
options: "a: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,b: You must yield the right-of-way.,c: Honk your horn to let them know you are there."
note: "Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times.  'Be careful when you are turning or backing up. This is particularly important if you are driving a hybrid or electric vehicle because blind pedestrians rely on sound to know there is a vehicle nearby.'"

question: Which of the following driving skills are affected by the use of alcohol and/or drugs?
options: "a: Alertness and concentration.,b: Reaction time and coordination.,c: All of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook states that alcohol and/or drugs affect 'your ability to drive safely and react to what you see and hear.'  This includes alertness and concentration, reaction time, and coordination."

question: When passing, you should move back into the right lane when:
options: "a: You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c: You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, you should move back into the right lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. 'Signal and return to your original lane.'"

question: If you have a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection, you should
options: "a: Enter the intersection and wait until traffic clears,b: Merge into another lane and try to go around the traffic,c: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears"
note: "Even if you have a green light, do not start across the intersection if there are pedestrians or vehicles blocking your pathway.  'It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.'"

question: You may make a left turn on a red light from:
options: "a: One-way street. onto a 2-way street,b: One-way street onto a one-way street.,c: Two-way street. onto a one-way street.
note: "You may turn left against a red light when you are turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists who have a green light. Look both ways and turn when it is safe."

question: Which of the following should you do if you are being followed by a tailgater?
options: "a: Change lanes and allow the tailgater to pass.,b: Tap the brakes to signal you are moving at a slower pace.,c: Increase your speed to match the speed of the vehicle."
note: "The DMV handbook recommends that you change lanes and allow the tailgater to pass when safe to do so. 'Maintain your course and speed. Then, when safe to do so, merge right to change into another lane and allow the tailgater to pass.'"

question: What is the best advice for driving when heavy fog or dust occurs?
options: "a: try not to drive until the conditions improve,b: do not drive too slowly because other drivers may hit you,c: alternate your low and high beams to improve visibility"
note: "The DMV Handbook states, 'It is best to avoid driving in heavy fog or smoke. Consider postponing your trip until the fog clears.'"

question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?
options: "a: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c: Stay in your lane slow down and let it pass."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Give the right-of-way to any law enforcement vehicle, fire engine, ambulance, or other emergency vehicle using a siren and red lights. Failure to pull over may result in a ticket. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle(s) have passed.'"

question: What is the first thing you should do if your wheels move off the pavement?
options: "a: Ease your foot off the gas pedal and brake gently,b: Pull over to the right and sound your horn to warn the other drivers,c: Pull the steering wheel back"
note: "According to page 68, the first step you should take if your wheels drift off the pavement is to 'Grip the steering wheel firmly. Remove your foot from the accelerator. Brake gently.'"

question: Where a left turn at an intersection can be started from either of two lanes, a U-turn can be started from
options: "a: Either of the two lanes,b: Only the left lane,c: Any lane that is open"
note: "According to page 20 of the DMV Handbook, 'To make a U-turn, signal and use the left turn lane or far-left lane.'"

question: Check your rearview mirrors:
options: "a: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b: To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,c: Only when you are slowing down."
note: "The text states, 'Knowing what is behind you can help you avoid rear-end collisions. Check traffic behind you often by using your rearview mirror, side mirrors, and turning your head when you: ... - Reduce your speed.' This clearly implies that checking rearview mirrors is essential for overall awareness of the road behind."

question: What happens if you do not signal when required?
options: "a: You may get a ticket,b: You may cause an accident,c: All of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states that it is important to signal when making a turn, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping, and that failing to do so could result in a ticket or cause an accident. The correct answer is all of the above."

question: If an oncoming vehicle has started to turn left in front of you
options: "a: Maintain your speed and take your right of way,b: Honk your horn to warn the driver and maintain your speed,c: Slow or stop to prevent a collision"
note: "When turning left, do not assume that an oncoming vehicle with its right turn signal on is turning before it reaches you. The driver may have their signal on by mistake or plan to turn just beyond you. Wait for the vehicle to start its turn before beginning the left turn."

question: You are driving at night on a dimly lit street and using high beams. You should dim your lights when you are within 500 feet of
options: "a: a vehicle approaching you from behind,b: an oncoming vehicle,c: a sharp curve or hill"
note: "According to page 11 of The DMV handbook, you should 'Dim your high-beam headlights to low beams within 500 feet of a vehicle coming toward you or within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.'"

question: You should not start across an intersection if you know you will...
options: "a: Block the intersection when the light turns red.,b: Unless you enter the intersection on a yellow light.,c: Unless you enter the intersection on a green light.,d: None of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 39: 'It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.'"

question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass another vehicle, you should:
options: "a: Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b: Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c: All of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Before you change lanes: Signal,  Check your mirrors, Check traffic behind and beside you, Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure the lane is clear, Check your blind spots for other vehicles, motorcyclists, and bicyclists. Do not let the vehicle drift into another lane.'"

question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching while using its siren and flashing lights. You should:
options: "a: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,b: Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,c: Continue through the intersection"
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Give the right-of-way to any law enforcement vehicle, fire engine, ambulance, or other emergency vehicle using a siren and red lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle(s) have passed.'"

question: You have been involved in a minor traffic collision with a parked vehicle and you can't find the owner. You must:
options: "a: Leave a note on the vehicle.,b: Report the collision without delay to the city police or,c: Both of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Try to find the owner if your vehicle hits or rolls into a parked car or other property. If you cannot find the owner, leave a note with your name, phone number, and address. Securely attach the note to the vehicle or property. Report the collision to law enforcement.'"

question: What is a likely effect when you take another drug while you drink alcohol?
options: "a: There are no effects unless the drug is prescription only,b: If the drug is over-the-counter there are no effects,c: The effects of the alcohol and the drug are enhanced"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 72, 'It is illegal to drive after… Using any combination of alcohol or drugs that decreases your ability to drive safely.'"

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:
options: "a: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c: Leave the front wheels straight."
note: "To prevent your vehicle from rolling backwards, turn the front wheels away from the curb (left towards the center of the road) and let your vehicle roll back a few inches. The wheel should gently touch the curb."

question: You must not cross a solid double line in the center of the roadway to
options: "a: Overtake and pass another vehicle,b: Make a left turn,c: Enter a private driveway"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Do not pass over double solid yellow lines... make a left turn... except at designated openings.'"

question: Driving under the influence of any medication which impairs your driving is permitted:
options: "a: Under no circumstances.,b: If you don't feel drowsy.,c: If it is prescribed by a physician."
note: "It is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.  'The law does not see a difference between illegal drugs and medications you get from a doctor or pharmacy. They can all affect your ability to drive safely and react to what you see and hear.' (Page 72)"

question: On a freeway, drivers should look farther ahead than they normally would on a city street
options: "a: Because it takes 500 feet to stop a vehicle on a freeway,b: In order to spot potential hazards and dangers ahead,c: Because there are multiple lanes"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'To give yourself time to react, avoid last minute moves and hazards, always keep your eyes moving and scan the road at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.'"

question: Make room for cars that are entering the freeway by:
options: "a: Slowing down.,b: Merging into a different lane.,c: Maintaining your speed and position."
note: "According to page 22, 'Make space for vehicles entering freeways, even if you have the right-of-way.'"

question: You may use your horn on narrow mountain roads
options: "a: To alert oncoming traffic where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead,b: To let pedestrians know you are there,c: To signal to other drivers that you are in a hurry"
note: "The DMV Handbook states on page 12: 'Use your vehicle's horn to let other drivers know you are there or warn others of a hazard. Use your horn to: Avoid collisions. Alert oncoming traffic on narrow mountain roads where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead.'"

question: When is it required to signal before changing lanes?
options: "a: At all times,b: Only when there are other vehicles nearby,c: Only when changing lanes on a freeway"
note: "The DMV Handbook states that you should 'Always signal when you turn, change lanes, slow down, or stop.'"

question: Which of the following is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: "a: A hilly,b: A residential road,c: A road in a shaded area"
note: "According to page 61, 'Shade from trees or buildings can hide icy spots on cold, wet days. These areas freeze first and dry out last.'"

question: It is against the law to enter an intersection or crosswalk when
options: "a: The light is yellow,b: The light is flashing red,c: You cannot cross without obstructing traffic from either side."
note: "The DMV Handbook states on page 39 that it is against the law to block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red."

question: Using a cell phone while operating a motor vehicle is considered a distraction because:
options: "a: It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,b: It occupies the driver's hands,c: It is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 70 'Cell phones are the main source of distracted driving. Driving while using a handheld cell phone is unsafe and illegal... It occupies the driver's hands.'"

question: At dawn or dusk and in rain or snow, it can be hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn:
options: "a: Up the instrumental panel lights.,b: On your parking lights.,c: On your headlights."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'Use your headlights: When it is too dark to see from 1,000 feet away, Beginning 30 minutes after sunset, Until 30 minutes before sunrise, In adverse weather. If you need to use your windshield wipers due to fog, rain, or snow, you must turn on your low-beam headlights.'"

question: Who is most at risk?
options: "a: Drivers who are fatigued,b: Drivers who are driving on long boring roads,c: All of the above"
note: "Page 9 of the California Driver's Handbook states 'Fatigue and Drowsiness - Can affect your vision and increase reaction time to hazards.'"

question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?
options: "a: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c: Stay in your lane slow down and let it pass."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Give the right-of-way to any law enforcement vehicle, fire engine, ambulance, or other emergency vehicle using a siren and red lights. Failure to pull over may result in a ticket. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle(s) have passed.'"

question: When both right and left turn signals are flashing at the same time on a moving vehicle, it means
options: "a: It is carrying children to or from school,b: Let the vehicle have the right-of-way,c: There may be a hazard or an accident ahead"
note: "If you can see a collision or hazard ahead, warn drivers behind you using these methods: Turn on your emergency flashers. Lightly tap your brake pedal three or four times. Use a hand signal when slowing and stopping."

question: What is the benefit of a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: "a: Other drivers can cut in front of you,b: If another driver makes a mistake,c: It inflates to protect you from injury in the case of a collision."
note: "A space cushion around your vehicle allows for you to react if another driver makes a mistake. The DMV Handbook states 'Following other vehicles at a safe distance gives you enough time to react if another driver makes a mistake.'"

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, you should:
options: "a: Grip the steering wheel firmly,b: Pump the brakes rapidly.,c: Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, if a tire blows out while you are driving, you should 'Hold the steering wheel with both hands. Maintain your vehicle speed if possible and safe. Gradually release the accelerator. Correct the steering as necessary to stabilize your vehicle and regain control.' "

question: To avoid glare from the headlights of an approaching car:
options: "a: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b: Stay focused on the centerline on the road.,c: Flash your high beams."
note: "To avoid glare from the headlights of an approaching car, the DMV handbook states on page 59, 'Do not look directly into the oncoming headlights...Look toward the right edge of your lane...Do not react to the other driver by keeping your high-beam headlights on.'"

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: "a: Another name for a four-way intersection.,b: An area designated for road construction workers.,c: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway."
note: "A crosswalk is the part of the road set aside for pedestrians to safely cross the road. They are often marked with white lines. School crossings may have yellow crosswalk lines. Not all crosswalks are marked. Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks."

question: It is unlawful to:
options: "a: Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,b: Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,c: Both of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 24, 'You must judge whether you have enough space to pass whenever you approach...a railroad crossing.' and, 'Do Not Pass...Within 100 feet of an intersection, bridge, tunnel, railroad crossing, or other hazardous area.'"

question: A safety zone is a specially marked area for passengers to get on or off buses or trolleys. You may not drive through a safety zone:
options: "a: Only when a bus or trolley is present.,b: Only when a bus or trolley is unloading passengers.,c: At any time or for any reason."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'Safety zones are spaces set aside for pedestrians waiting for buses, streetcars, and trolleys. Safety zones are marked by raised buttons or markers on a road. Do not drive through a safety zone under any condition.'"

question: When you see a NEV ROUTE sign, you should watch out for
options: "a: A Nevada law enforcement officer,b: Slow-moving vehicles in the roadway,c: Animal-drawn vehicles"
note: "On page 45, the DMV Handbook states, 'Watch for slow-moving vehicles when you see these signs or markings: - NEV USE ONLY - NEV ROUTE. NEVs and LSVs reach a maximum speed of 25 mph.'"

question: Which of the following roadways freeze first when wet?
options: "a: Bridges and overpasses,b: Intersections,c: Tunnels"
note: "Bridges and overpasses tend to freeze before the rest of the road because they can have icy spots."

question: If you are involved in a traffic collision and no one is injured, you are required to complete and submit a written report to
options: "a: DMV,b: CHP,c: EDD"
note: "According to the California Driver's Handbook, page 77, 'If you are in a collision, you must report it to DMV within 10 days if:  - The collision caused more than $1,000 in damage to property. - Anyone was injured or killed.'"

question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:
options: "a: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,b: Inconvenience drivers.,c: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones."
note: "Cones, drums, and barriers are used to keep traffic out of a hazardous work zone. 'Go through the work zone carefully by: Slowing down.' 'Cones, drums, or other barriers will guide you through the work zone.' "

question: When driving at night, you should:
options: "a: Always use your high beams.,b: Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c: Increase your following distance."
note: "When driving at night, you should increase your following distance. This gives you more time to react if the driver in front of you brakes suddenly."

question: Children on bicycles should be given extra space by motor vehicle operators because:
options: "a: They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,b: They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,c: Both of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook explains that motorcyclists are smaller and harder to see in blind spots, and they are less protected on the road. This applies to children on bikes as well. "

question: Which of these statements about drugs and traffic is true?
options: "a: Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving,b: Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don’t feel drowsy,c: Only illegal drugs can impair your driving"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Prescription and over-the-counter medications can make you an unsafe driver. Some medicines can make you sleepy. It is your responsibility to know the effects of the medications you take.'"

question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp where there is no acceleration lane, you should:
options: "a: Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match the flow of traffic.,b: Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c: Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'When you enter a highway, you will need to...Be at or near the speed of traffic...Merge into highway traffic when safe to do so. Do not stop unless absolutely necessary.'"

question: At a T-intersection with no signs or signals, you must yield to
options: "a: Traffic on the road you are entering,b: Traffic on the road you are leaving,c: Pedestrians in the crosswalk,d: None of the above"
note: "According to page 38, 'Vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians on the through road (continuing to go straight) have the right-of-way.' This means that the vehicle entering the T-intersection must yield to traffic on the road it is leaving."

question: Prior to entering a curve:
options: "a: Activate your turn signal.,b: Reduce your speed.,c: Brake hard."
note: "You must slow down before entering a curve to avoid losing control of your vehicle."

question: What happens if you do not signal when required?
options: "a: You may get a ticket,b: You may cause an accident,c: All of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states that it is important to signal when making a turn, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping, and that failing to do so could result in a ticket or cause an accident. The correct answer is all of the above."

question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signals:
options: "a: Only when pulling away from the curb.,b: When pulling next to but not away from the curb.,c: When pulling next to or away from the curb."
note: "According to the California Driver's Handbook, 'You should signal: ... Before pulling next to the curb or away from the curb.'"

question: If you have had several beers, the effects of alcohol will be reduced only by:
options: "a: Taking a cold shower.,b: Waiting several hours.,c: Drinking several cups of coffee."
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Almost everyone feels negative effects of alcohol, even at levels lower than the legal limit.’ Therefore, the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol is to wait several hours."

question: A U-turn is not permitted:
options: "a: In a parking lot.,b: On or near any curve or hill.,c: On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions."
note: "The DMV handbook states that you cannot make a U-turn 'When you cannot see clearly for 200 feet in each direction.' (Page 20).  Therefore, a U-turn is not permitted on or near any curve or hill."

question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:
options: "a: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b: The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c: Other drivers when they want to slow down."
note: "'Large vehicles and commercial trucks take longer to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed. When traveling, they create extra space in front of their vehicle to use if they need to stop suddenly.'"

question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: "a: You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,b: You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,c: You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic."
note: "A yellow arrow means the protected turning time is ending. The signal will change soon. If you cannot stop safely or you are already in the intersection, cautiously complete your turn. Pay attention to the next signal. It could be a: - Green or red traffic signal light. - Red arrow."

question: When passing another vehicle:
options: "a: Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,b: Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,c: Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible."
note: "The DMV handbook states that when passing another vehicle, you should 'speed up to pass the vehicle.' This means that you should pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible."

question: What usually causes a locked wheel skid?
options: "a: Braking too hard at a slow speed,b: Braking lightly at a slow speed,c: Braking too hard at a fast speed"
note: "A locked wheel skid is usually caused by braking too hard when you are going too fast. 'A locked wheel skid is usually caused by braking too hard when you are going too fast.'"

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn:
options: "a: They may use the left lane.,b: They may cut through all lanes.,c: They may wait on the side of the road."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Bicyclists may… make left and right turns in the same way drivers do, using hand signals and turn lanes.'"

question: To avoid last minute moves, you should be looking down the road to where your vehicle will be in about
options: "a: 5 to 10 seconds,b: 10 to 15 seconds,c: 15 to 20 seconds"
note: "The DMV handbook says 'To give yourself time to react, avoid last minute moves and hazards, always keep your eyes moving and scan the road at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.'"

question: The maximum posted speed limit should be driven only:
options: "a: During the night.,b: During the day.,c: Under ideal conditions."
note: "The DMV handbook states that you may never drive faster than is safe for the current road conditions. 'This is known as the Basic Speed Law. Make sure you manage your speed and slow down when conditions call for it.'"

question: You should not drive
options: "a: After you have taken any drink drug or medication which changes how you think or act or causes you to be less careful,b: If you are not alert,c: Both of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.'  It also mentions, 'You must be alert to quickly decide the correct course of action in any type of traffic situation, including unexpected ones.'"

question: If you are leaving a parking lot, you
options: "a: Must turn either left or right only when it is safe,b: Have the right-of-way,c: Must yield to traffic before re-entering the road"
note: "When entering traffic from a full stop, signal and leave a large enough space to get up to the speed of traffic.  To merge, enter, or exit traffic, you need a space that is:  - Half a block on city streets, which is about 150 feet.  - A full block on the highway, which is about 300 feet."

question: You must stop at the intersection ahead. Just before the intersection, you have to cross railroad tracks. You should stop before crossing the railroad tracks when:
options: "a: There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b: The crossing is located in a city or town with frequent train traffic.,c: You are transporting two or more children in a passenger vehicle."
note: "According to the DMV handbook on page 51, 'Never stop on the railroad tracks. Wait and do not begin proceeding if you do not have enough room to completely cross the tracks. If you are on the tracks, you risk injury or death.'"

question: In a vehicle equipped with airbags, the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride is in:
options: "a: The front seat.,b: The back seat.,c: The bed of a pick-up truck."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Children who are under 8 years old, or who are less than 4 feet 9 inches tall: Secure in a child passenger restraint system in a rear seat.'"

question: Sleeping pills, tranquilizers, pain medicine, or cold or allergy medications
options: "a: May impair your driving,b: May increase the bad effects of alcohol on your driving,c: Both of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Prescription and over-the-counter medications can make you an unsafe driver.'  It also states that 'Some medicines can make you sleepy.'  Therefore, the answer is 'c', as the medications can impair driving and increase the negative effects of alcohol."

question: On a green arrow, you must:
options: "a: Yield to any vehicle,b: Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.,c: Wait four seconds before proceeding."
note: "A green arrow means GO in the direction the arrow is pointing. The green arrow allows you to make a protected turn. Oncoming vehicles are stopped by a red traffic signal light. "

question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are not easy to see; therefore, you should:
options: "a: Slow down when driving.,b: Make constant visual checks.,c: Share a lane with a motorcycle."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Motorcycles are smaller in size and harder to see so they easily disappear in vehicle blind spots.'"

question: Regulatory signs are:
options: "a: Green.,b: Yellow.,c: White."
note: "The answer is 'c' White.  This is stated on page 37 of the DMV handbook.  'Red And White Regulatory Sign, Follow the sign's instruction.'"

question: When passing, you should move back into the right lane when:
options: "a: You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c: You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, you should move back into the right lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. 'Signal and return to your original lane.'"

question: Which of these statements is true about roadwork zones?
options: "a: Fines are the same for violations committed in work zones as they are under normal traffic conditions.,b: You must ‘Slow for the Cone Zone’,c: Slow down only if you think workers are present."
note: "The DMV Handbook states that drivers should 'Slow for the Cone Zone.' (page 49)"

question: A safety zone is a specially marked area for passengers to get on or off buses or trolleys. You may not drive through a safety zone:
options: "a: Only when a bus or trolley is present.,b: Only when a bus or trolley is unloading passengers.,c: At any time or for any reason."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'Safety zones are spaces set aside for pedestrians waiting for buses, streetcars, and trolleys. Safety zones are marked by raised buttons or markers on a road. Do not drive through a safety zone under any condition.'"

question: At an intersection with stop signs at all four (or more) corners, when two cars arrive at the same time you must yield the right-of-way to the driver
options: "a: On your right,b: On your left,c: Signaling a turn"
note: "The DMV handbook states: 'If a vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist gets to the intersection at the same time as you, give the right-of-way to the vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist on your right.'"

question: Which of these vehicles must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: "a: Tank trucks with hazardous materials placards.,b: Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat trailer.,c: Sport utility vehicles carrying four or more persons."
note: "According to page 50, 'Vehicles with these signs must stop before crossing railroad tracks.'"

question: When is it required for you to obey directions from a crossing guard?
options: "a: At all times.,b: During school hours only.,c: Only when children are present in front of a school."
note: "The DMV handbook states that you should 'Be sure to obey their directions at all times.' when referring to school safety patrols or crossing guards."

question: ABS is the acronym for
options: "a: Anti-lock Brake System,b: Anti-Braking System,c: Asphalt-Braking System"
note: "On page 60 of The DMV handbook, it states: 'To get out of a locked wheel skid if your vehicle is equipped with: Four-wheel antilock braking system (ABS), apply firm pressure on the brake pedal.'"

question: You are getting ready to make a right turn. You should:
options: "a: Signal and turn immediately.,b: Stop before entering the right lane and let all other traffic go first.,c: Slow down or stop"
note: "To make a right turn, drive close to the right edge of the road. If a designated right turn lane is available, enter at the opening.  Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn. Look over your right shoulder and reduce your speed. Stop behind the limit line. If there is no limit line, stop before you enter the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before you enter the intersection."

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: "a: Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,b: Be constantly alert.,c: Both of the above."
note: "Interstate driving requires drivers to 'Be aware of your surroundings' and  'Manage your speed' which are both required to drive safely at increased speeds. The DMV handbook provides the following in the section 'Be Aware Of Your Surroundings' on Page 57:  'To drive safely, you need to know what is around you. This helps you make good decisions and react to hazards on the road.'"

question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should drive:
options: "a: Near the right-hand side of the road.,b: Near the centerline.,c: On the left of the centerline."
note: "To make a left turn, you should drive 'close to the center divider or into the left turn lane.'"

question: What should you do if a pedestrian is still in the crosswalk after the 'DON'T WALK' sign begins to flash and your light has turned green?
options: "a: Wait until the pedestrian is out of your path before proceeding.,b: Wait until the pedestrian signals that it is okay for you to proceed.,c: Wait until the pedestrian has crossed the street completely before proceeding."
note: "Even if the 'DON'T WALK' sign is flashing and your light has turned green, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk. The DMV handbook states, 'Drivers must yield to pedestrians, even if the DON'T WALK light is flashing.'"

question: Various traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are the color:
options: "a: Red.,b: Orange.,c: Yellow."
note: "Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are typically orange. The DMV Handbook states:'Highway Construction and Maintenance Signs'. The signs shown in the image have black lettering and symbols on an orange background."

question: Bicycle riders must
options: "a: Ride facing traffic when there is no bike lane,b: Be given a safe amount of space when being passed by automobile drivers,c: Never walk the bicycle across the street"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'When you cannot change lanes to pass a bicyclist, allow at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicyclist. If you cannot give three feet of space, do not pass the cyclist until three feet of clearance can be given. This will help you avoid putting the bicyclist in danger.'"

question: Roadways are least slippery
options: "a: on bridges and freezing temperatures,b: after it has been raining for a while,c: during the first rain after a dry spell"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 61, 'When it starts to rain, the pavement can be very slippery. Slow down at the first sign of rain, drizzle, or snow on the road. This is especially true if it has been dry and hot for some time, because oil and dust on the road's surface have not been washed away.'"

question: To avoid last minute moves, you should be looking down the road to where your vehicle will be in about
options: "a: 5 to 10 seconds,b: 10 to 15 seconds,c: 15 to 20 seconds"
note: "The DMV handbook says 'To give yourself time to react, avoid last minute moves and hazards, always keep your eyes moving and scan the road at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.'"

question: California's "Basic Speed Law" says you must:
options: "a: Keep your speed close to that of other traffic.,b: Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.,c: Always drive at the posted speed limit."
note: "The Basic Speed Law states that you may never drive faster than is safe for the current road conditions. 'In California, you may never drive faster than is safe for the current road conditions. This is known as the Basic Speed Law.' (page 67)"

question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: "a: Cross the centerline in an intersection.,b: Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,c: Check for other drivers moving into the same lane."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 14: 'Never change lanes over double solid white lines. Wait until you see a single broken white line.'"

question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?
options: "a: A school crossing,b: A No Passing Zone,c: Yield"
note: "Pennant-shaped signs are no-passing zone signs. They are yellow with black lettering and are placed on the left side of two-way roads to warn drivers that passing is not safe in that area."

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: "a: Reduce your speed.,b: Traffic light ahead.,c: Do not pass."
note: "A single solid yellow line marks the center of a road with two-way traffic. Do not pass a vehicle in front of you if there is only one lane of traffic going your direction and a solid yellow line on your side of the road."

question: When driving in work zones, you should:
options: "a: Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b: Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 49, 'Go through the work zone carefully by: ... Allowing extra space between vehicles.'"

question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with its red lights flashing must remain stopped until:
options: "a: All students are off the bus.,b: The stop arm is retracted.,c: The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 50, 'When the bus flashes red lights (located at the top, front, and back of the bus), you must stop from either direction until the children are safely across the street and the lights stop flashing. Remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.'"

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:
options: "a: Stop,b: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c: Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Before entering an intersection, look left, right, and ahead to check for vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Be prepared to slow down and stop if necessary.'"

question: You are driving on the freeway. The vehicle in front of you is a large truck. You should drive
options: "a: Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead,b: Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle to be out of the truck drivers blind spot,c: No more than one car length behind the truck,d: None of the above"
note: "Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle to be out of the truck drivers blind spot'. This is emphasized in the 'Blind Spots (The No Zone)' section of The DMV handbook on page 42: 'If you cannot see the truck's side mirrors, the truck driver cannot see you.'"

question: You should not drive
options: "a: After you have taken any drink drug or medication which changes how you think or act or causes you to be less careful,b: If you are not alert,c: Both of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.'  It also mentions, 'You must be alert to quickly decide the correct course of action in any type of traffic situation, including unexpected ones.'"

question: You are driving in the far right lane of a four-lane freeway and notice thick broken white lines on the left side of your lane. You are driving in:
options: "a: The carpool lane and must merge into the next lane.,b: A special lane for slow-moving vehicles.,c: An exit lane."
note: "According to page 14, 'Ending freeway and street lanes are usually marked with large broken lines. If you are driving in a lane marked with broken lines, be prepared to exit the freeway or for the lane to end.'"

question: If there is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:
options: "a: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b: Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing."
note: "Pedestrians always have the right-of-way, even in unmarked crosswalks. 'Before entering an intersection, look left, right, and ahead to check for vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Be prepared to slow down and stop if necessary. Pedestrians always have the right-of-way.'"

question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, creating a hazard. What should you do first?
options: "a: Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b: Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c: Swerve into the lane next to you."
note: "The best initial reaction is to 'Take your foot off the gas pedal.' This creates space between you and the vehicle ahead, allowing you to assess the situation and react appropriately.  The DMV handbook states, 'If a vehicle merges in front of you too closely, take your foot off the accelerator.'"

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn:
options: "a: They may use the left lane.,b: They may cut through all lanes.,c: They may wait on the side of the road."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Bicyclists may… make left and right turns in the same way drivers do, using hand signals and turn lanes.'"

question: In which of the following scenarios should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: "a: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c: When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 27 that when parked on a hill or sloping driveway, your wheels should be turned so the vehicle will not roll into the street. This is to prevent the vehicle from rolling if the brakes fail."

question: If you must park your vehicle in an area not usually used for parking:
options: "a: Park with your reverse lights on.,b: Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c: Park five feet from the curb."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'If you cannot get completely off the road, stop where people can see you and your vehicle from behind.'  This means your vehicle must be visible from any direction to avoid collisions with other drivers."

question: If weather or light conditions require you to have your lights on while driving:
options: "a: Use your parking lights.,b: Use your high beams.,c: Use your low beams."
note: "According to page 11, 'Use your headlights: ...If you need to use your windshield wipers due to fog, rain, or snow, you must turn on your low-beam headlights.'"

question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, drivers should:
options: "a: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c: Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'You may drive on or cross a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway or alley.'  This means drivers should stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area."

question: If you want to enter the freeway but you don't see a gap in traffic, you should:
options: "a: Maintain your speed and force the other drivers to create a gap.,b: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.,c: Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap."
note: "You should 'Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.' as stated on page 23 of the DMV Handbook. It says that when entering a highway, you should 'Be at or near the speed of traffic... Merge into highway traffic when safe to do so. Do not stop unless absolutely necessary.'"

question: How should bicyclists signal a turn?
options: "a: Using their vehicle's signal lights,b: Using hand and arm positions,c: Using their horn"
note: "Bicyclists may signal a turn with their arm held straight out, pointing in the direction they plan to turn.  This information is located on page 10 of The DMV handbook."

question: With a Class C driver's license, a person may drive
options: "a: a light rail train,b: car or van or pickup truck,c: semi truck"
note: "On page 7, The DMV handbook states 'Most people need a noncommercial Class C driver's license.'  On page 1, it states 'For information on vehicles covered by a Class C, visit dmv.ca.gov/dl.'"

question: It is against the law to enter an intersection or crosswalk when
options: "a: The light is yellow,b: The light is flashing red,c: You cannot cross without obstructing traffic from either side."
note: "The DMV Handbook states on page 39 that it is against the law to block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red."

question: Coasting with the gear shift in neutral is
options: "a: Recommended in the mountains,b: Safe and conserves gas,c: Against the law"
note: "Coasting with the gear shift in neutral is against the law. 'Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.' This is a dangerous practice."

question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:
options: "a: Press down hard on the accelerator.,b: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c: Set the parking brake."
note: "Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, it is crucial to be aware of your surroundings to make safe driving decisions. The DMV handbook states that you should check your mirrors for surrounding traffic before entering an intersection."

question: Pedestrians crossing at corners have the right-of-way:
options: "a: Only at controlled intersections.,b: Only when a crosswalk is painted on the street.,c: Whether or not a crosswalk is marked."
note: "Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks. 'Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks.'"

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: "a: Another name for a four-way intersection.,b: An area designated for road construction workers.,c: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway."
note: "A crosswalk is the part of the road set aside for pedestrians to safely cross the road. They are often marked with white lines. School crossings may have yellow crosswalk lines. Not all crosswalks are marked. Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks."

question: Streets and highways are most slippery:
options: "a: When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b: When they are clean and dry.,c: Just after it starts to rain."
note: "The DMV Handbook states 'When it starts to rain, the pavement can be very slippery.' This is because oil and dust on the road surface have not been washed away. "

question: You should turn on your headlights:
options: "a: One half hour after sunset.,b: When stopped at a railroad crossing.,c: When parked at a school."
note: "The DMV Handbook states, 'Use your headlights: Beginning 30 minutes after sunset. Until 30 minutes before sunrise.'"

question: A pentagon-shaped sign is a:
options: "a: Stop sign.,b: Regulatory sign.,c: School zone or school crossing sign."
note: "The DMV handbook states that a 5-sided sign indicates a school zone or school crossing."

question: When making a right turn from a highway with two lanes traveling in your direction, you may turn from:
options: "a: The lane closest to the center of the road.,b: The lane nearest the curb or edge of the roadway.,c: Either lane"
note: "According to the DMV handbook, when making a right turn from a highway with two lanes traveling in your direction, you may turn from 'the lane nearest the curb or edge of the roadway'."

question: Which of the following is not a safe driving practice when driving on the interstate?
options: "a: Slower traffic must keep to the right.,b: Change lanes without signaling.,c: If you miss your exit"
note: "The DMV handbook states 'Stay in one lane as much as possible. Do not weave in and out of traffic. Last minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.'  Changing lanes without signaling is not a safe driving practice, and it is not allowed on the interstate."

question: Any driver who willfully flees or attempts to evade law enforcement, during which a person is seriously injured, is subject to:
options: "a: Imprisonment in a state prison for up to seven years.,b: A fine of less than $1000.,c: Attending an anger-management class."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'A person convicted of causing serious bodily injury during a law enforcement pursuit is subject to imprisonment in a state prison for up to seven years, or a county jail for one year or less.'"

question: Which of these is considered a common cause of collision?
options: "a: Unsafe speed,b: Not following stop signs signals and signs,c: All the above"
note: "The DMV handbook lists 'Unsafe speed', 'Improper turns', 'Not following the right-of-way rules', 'Not following stop signals and signs', 'Driving on the wrong side of the road', 'A vehicle traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic' as common causes of collisions. Therefore, 'all the above' is the correct answer."

question: Excessive speed:
options: "a: Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b: Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c: Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death."
note: "Excessive speed is a main cause of collisions, which could result in death or serious injury. 'The most common causes of collisions are: Driver distractions. Unsafe speed. Improper turns.
