Not following the right-of-way rules. Not following stop signals and signs. Driving on the wrong side of the road. A vehicle traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.'"

question: When driving at night with no other vehicles ahead, a driver should use
options: "a: High beam lights,b: Low-beam lights,c: Parking lights"
note: "When driving at night with no other vehicles ahead, a driver should use high-beam headlights. 'When driving at night, use your high-beam headlights on open country roads or dark city streets.'"

question: Any driver who willfully flees or attempts to evade law enforcement, during which a person is seriously injured, is subject to:
options: "a: Imprisonment in a state prison for up to seven years.,b: A fine of less than $1000.,c: Attending an anger-management class."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'A person convicted of causing serious bodily injury during a law enforcement pursuit is subject to imprisonment in a state prison for up to seven years, or a county jail for one year or less.'"

question: You should not start across an intersection if you know you will...
options: "a: Block the intersection when the light turns red.,b: Unless you enter the intersection on a yellow light.,c: Unless you enter the intersection on a green light.,d: None of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 39: 'It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.'"

question: You should use your turn signals...
options: "a: When changing lanes or merging into traffic.,b: When turning left or right.,c: Both of the above.,d: None of the above"
note: "The DMV Handbook states that you should 'Always signal when you turn, change lanes, slow down, or stop.'  This includes both turning left or right and changing lanes or merging."

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must
options: "a: Slow down because the road ends,b: Be prepared for workers and slow moving equipment,c: Change lanes and maintain speed"
note: "You will see warning signs and message boards when there are workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes ahead.  Go through the work zone carefully by: Slowing down, Allowing extra space between vehicles, Expecting sudden slowing or stopping, Watching for drivers changing lanes, Avoiding distractions."

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing in the middle of the street instead of in a crosswalk, you:
options: "a: Must stop for them.,b: Do not have to stop for them.,c: Should honk your horn at them."
note: "Even though they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.  'When there is a pedestrian crossing a roadway with or without a crosswalk, you **must** use caution, reduce your speed, or stop to allow the pedestrian to safely finish crossing.'"

question: You are driving on the freeway and need to exit. You should:
options: "a: Use your turn signal and move into the exit lane,b: Exit immediately without signaling,c: Accelerate into the exit lane,d: None of the above"
note: "To exit a highway safely, you should know your exit and be aware of when it is approaching. If you plan to change lanes, do so one at a time. Signal and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots. When in the proper lane, signal five seconds (approximately 400 feet) before you exit."

question: How can you prevent fatigue on a long trip?
options: "a: Get enough sleep,b: Plan to drive long trips with a companion,c: All of the above"
note: "Page 9 of the DMV handbook states 'Fatigue and Drowsiness - Can affect your vision and increase reaction time to hazards.'"

question: What color curb does not allow vehicles to stop or park?
options: "a: Yellow.,b: Red.,c: White."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Red: No stopping, standing, or parking.'"

question: If you become sleepy while driving, it is best to
options: "a: Increase your speed to get away from other vehicles,b: Move over to the right lane and continue driving,c: Drive to a safe place stop and rest"
note: "It is stated on page 9 that 'Fatigue and Drowsiness - Can affect your vision and increase reaction time to hazards.' The best solution is to 'Drive to a safe place, stop and rest.'"

question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas:
options: "a: Have a red background with green writing.,b: Have an orange background with black writing.,c: Have a yellow background with blue writing."
note: "The DMV handbook states on Page 36 that 'Diamond-Shaped Sign Warns you of specific road conditions and dangers ahead.'"

question: What happens if you do not signal when required?
options: "a: You may get a ticket,b: You may cause an accident,c: All of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states that it is important to signal when making a turn, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping, and that failing to do so could result in a ticket or cause an accident. The correct answer is all of the above."

question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:
options: "a: Stay in the right lane as much as possible because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.,b: Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder so that you can pass.,c: Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass."
note: "To safely pass a motorcycle that is in the travel lane you may need to change to another lane. In this case, pass safely then return to your original lane. Leave space between your vehicle and the bicyclist."

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the surface of the road, you should:
options: "a: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c: Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'If your vehicle starts to hydroplane: Slow down gradually. Do not use the brakes. Sudden braking may cause you to lose control of your vehicle.'"

question: Parallel parking is when the
options: "a: Front wheels are turned toward the street,b: Vehicle is in line with other parked vehicles,c: Rear wheels are touching the curb"
note: "Parallel parking is defined as parking 'in line with the road and other parked vehicles'.  The DMV handbook states that on page 26: 'Parallel parking is when you park in line with the road and other parked vehicles.'"

question: Blind spots are:
options: "a: Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,b: Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,c: Traffic control devices."
note: "Blind spots are 'areas around the vehicle that a driver cannot see when looking straight ahead or using the mirrors.' (Page 58)"

question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:
options: "a: Hazards.,b: Vehicles.,c: Dangerous."
note: "Bicycles are considered 'vehicles' on roadways and share the same rights and responsibilities as other vehicles. This is clearly stated on page 46, where The DMV handbook says 'Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other drivers.'"

question: You are approaching a green traffic light and traffic is blocking the intersection. What is the best thing to do?
options: "a: Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b: Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c: Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear."
note: "Even if you have a green light, do not start across the intersection if there are pedestrians or vehicles blocking your pathway.  It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red."

question: To know where traffic is behind you:
options: "a: Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b: Turn and look out your back window.,c: Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 58, 'Knowing what is behind you can help you avoid rear-end collisions. Check traffic behind you often by using your rearview mirror, side mirrors, and turning your head when you: ... reduce your speed.'"

question: When you prepare to make a left turn from a one-way road into a one-way road, you must
options: "a: Move into the left lane or to the left side of a single lane,b: Move into the right lane or to the right side of a single lane,c: Move into the right lane or to the left side of a single lane"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'To turn left: Drive close to the center divider or into the left turn lane.' On a one-way street, you should be driving in the far left lane, so to turn left you should remain in that lane."

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:
options: "a: Passing is permitted from the left.,b: Passing is permitted from the right.,c: Passing is not permitted from either direction."
note: "Double solid yellow lines indicate a lane barrier and passing is not permitted from either direction. 'Do not pass over double solid yellow lines.'"

question: You are driving a slow moving vehicle on a winding two-lane highway. You must pull over when it is safe and let other drivers pass when you are followed by
options: "a: 3 vehicles,b: 4 vehicles,c: 5 or more vehicles"
note: "According to the DMV handbook, ‘You must use a turnout area or lane to let other vehicles pass when you are driving slowly on a two-lane road, where passing is unsafe, and there are five or more vehicles following you.'"

question: You drive defensively when you:
options: "a: Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b: Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c: Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards."
note: "Defensive driving is described as being aware of your surroundings, and the DMV handbook states that 'To drive safely, you need to know what is around you.'"

question: What is the first thing you should do if your wheels move off the pavement?
options: "a: Ease your foot off the gas pedal and brake gently,b: Pull over to the right and sound your horn to warn the other drivers,c: Pull the steering wheel back"
note: "According to page 68, the first step you should take if your wheels drift off the pavement is to 'Grip the steering wheel firmly. Remove your foot from the accelerator. Brake gently.'"

question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:
options: "a: Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b: Must yield to vehicles only on your right.,c: Should slow down but never stop."
note: "According to the DMV handbook on page 38, 'Slow down and be ready to stop to let any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian pass before you proceed.'"

question: If you come to a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights, you should:
options: "a: Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.,b: Come to a complete stop well behind the gates,c: Slow down and drive around the gates."
note: "When the crossing devices or a person warns you a train is coming, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest track."

question: The first thing that alcohol effects is:
options: "a: Vision.,b: Judgment.,c: Balance."
note: "The DMV handbook states that alcohol can 'affect your ability to drive safely and react to what you see and hear.'"

question: When driving in work zones, you should:
options: "a: Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.,b: Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c: Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Go through the work zone carefully by: Slowing down., Allowing extra space between vehicles., Expecting sudden slowing or stopping.'"

question: The traffic light is green and you want to drive straight through an intersection. If a car is already in the intersection and is making a turn, you must
options: "a: Enter the intersection and then stop,b: Drive through the intersection. You have the right-of-way,c: Let that car complete its turn before you enter the intersection"
note: "Even if you have a green light, you must still yield to vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection. 'You should still stop for any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian in the intersection. Only proceed if you have enough space without creating a danger to any oncoming vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian.' "

question: When should you signal?
options: "a: Before turning 100 feet before turning.,b: 2100 feet before turning.,c: 3200 feet before turning.,d: none of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states that drivers should signal 'At least 100 feet before you turn.'"

question: You want to pass a bicyclist in a narrow traffic lane when an oncoming vehicle is approaching. You should:
options: "a: Honk your horn then pass the bicyclist.,b: Slow down and let the vehicle pass you before you pass the bicyclist.,c: Wait until the bicyclist rides off the roadway."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'When you cannot change lanes to pass a bicyclist, allow at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicyclist.'  Therefore, the best approach is to slow down and allow the oncoming vehicle to pass before attempting to pass the bicyclist."

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
options: "a: Challenge them.,b: Get out of their way.,c: Speed up."
note: "The best course of action when encountering an aggressive driver is to get out of their way.  'If a tailgater is behind you. Maintain your course and speed. Then, when safe to do so, merge right to change into another lane and allow the tailgater to pass.'"

question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:
options: "a: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,b: Inconvenience drivers.,c: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones."
note: "Cones, drums, and barriers are used to keep traffic out of a hazardous work zone. 'Go through the work zone carefully by: Slowing down.' 'Cones, drums, or other barriers will guide you through the work zone.' "

question: You want to pass a bicyclist riding on the right edge of your lane. You
options: "a: must honk your horn before passing the bicyclist,b: must not squeeze past the bicyclist,c: may not pass the bicyclist for any reason"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'When you cannot change lanes to pass a bicyclist, allow at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicyclist. If you cannot give three feet of space, do not pass the cyclist until three feet of clearance can be given.'"

question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: "a: Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,b: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c: The speed at which you drive a vehicle does not affect safety."
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'You must drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. At the same time, you should not block normal and reasonable traffic flow by driving too slowly. If you drive faster or slower than the speed limit, you may be cited.'"

question: You may make a left turn on a red light only from a:
options: "a: One-way street onto a two-way street.,b: One-way street onto a one-way street.,c: Two-way street onto a one-way street."
note: "You may turn left against a red light when you are turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists who have a green light. Look both ways and turn when it is safe."

question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should:
options: "a: Turn into any lane.,b: Turn into first lane.,c: Turn into second lane."
note: "According to page 21 of the DMV handbook, 'If there are three or more lanes in your direction of travel, you may end your turn in any lane that is open.'"

question: You may pass a vehicle when:
options: "a: You are on a hill or curve.,b: You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane."
note: "A broken yellow line indicates you may pass if the broken line is next to your driving lane. Only pass when it is safe."

question: A pentagon-shaped sign is a:
options: "a: Stop sign.,b: Regulatory sign.,c: School zone or school crossing sign."
note: "The DMV handbook states that a 5-sided sign indicates a school zone or school crossing."

question: Which of the following is true about roadways on bridges and overpasses in cold, wet weather?
options: "a: They tend to freeze before the rest of the road does.,b: They do not freeze because they are made of concrete.,c: They tend to freeze after the rest of the road does."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Bridges and overpasses tend to freeze before the rest of the road.'"

question: You must file a report of a traffic accident occurring in California when:
options: "a: Your vehicle fails a smog test.,b: You are involved in a collision and there is an injury.,c: You change your insurance company."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 77, 'You must report it to DMV within 10 days if: - The collision caused more than $1,000 in damage to property. - Anyone was injured or killed. This applies even if the injuries were minor.'"

question: If weather or light conditions require you to have your lights on while driving:
options: "a: Use your parking lights.,b: Use your high beams.,c: Use your low beams."
note: "According to page 11, 'Use your headlights: ...If you need to use your windshield wipers due to fog, rain, or snow, you must turn on your low-beam headlights.'"

question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: "a: You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,b: You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,c: You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic."
note: "A yellow arrow means the protected turning time is ending. The signal will change soon. If you cannot stop safely or you are already in the intersection, cautiously complete your turn. Pay attention to the next signal. It could be a: - Green or red traffic signal light. - Red arrow."

question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:
options: "a: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,b: Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.,c: Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking."
note: "You should always slow down before entering a curve, especially one that is downhill. 'Slow down as you approach intersections and curves. For sharp curves, slow down as you approach and move through.'"

question: If there is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:
options: "a: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b: Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing."
note: "Pedestrians always have the right-of-way, even in unmarked crosswalks. 'Before entering an intersection, look left, right, and ahead to check for vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Be prepared to slow down and stop if necessary. Pedestrians always have the right-of-way.'"

question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.
options: "a: Drinking caffeine,b: Eating foods high in fat,c: Time"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Only time can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.'"

question: You must file a report of a traffic accident occurring in California when:
options: "a: Your vehicle fails a smog test.,b: You are involved in a collision and there is an injury.,c: You change your insurance company."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 77, 'You must report it to DMV within 10 days if: - The collision caused more than $1,000 in damage to property. - Anyone was injured or killed. This applies even if the injuries were minor.'"

question: On a freeway, drivers should look farther ahead than they normally would on a city street
options: "a: Because it takes 500 feet to stop a vehicle on a freeway,b: In order to spot potential hazards and dangers ahead,c: Because there are multiple lanes"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'To give yourself time to react, avoid last minute moves and hazards, always keep your eyes moving and scan the road at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.'"

question: The three-second rule applies to the space ______ of your vehicle.
options: "a: To the sides,b: Ahead,c: In the back"
note: "The 'three-second rule' is a driving rule that helps you estimate how closely you should follow other vehicles.  'When the vehicle in front of you passes a certain point, such as a sign, count three seconds. If you pass the same point before you finish counting, you are following too closely.'"

question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp where there is no acceleration lane, you should:
options: "a: Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match the flow of traffic.,b: Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c: Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'When you enter a highway, you will need to...Be at or near the speed of traffic...Merge into highway traffic when safe to do so. Do not stop unless absolutely necessary.'"

question: You may make a left turn on a red light only from a:
options: "a: One-way street onto a two-way street.,b: One-way street onto a one-way street.,c: Two-way street onto a one-way street."
note: "You may turn left against a red light when you are turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists who have a green light. Look both ways and turn when it is safe."

question: Which of these statements is true about drugs and driving?
options: "a: Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,b: Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c: Only illegal drugs can impair your driving."
note: "The DMV Handbook states that 'The law does not see a difference between illegal drugs and medications you get from a doctor or pharmacy. They can all affect your ability to drive safely and react to what you see and hear.'"

question: You must stop at the intersection ahead. Just before the intersection, you have to cross railroad tracks. You should stop before you cross the railroad tracks when
options: "a: You don’t have room to completely cross the tracks,b: The crossing is located in a city or town with frequent train traffic,c: You transport two or more children in a passenger vehicle"
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Never stop on the railroad tracks. Wait and do not begin proceeding if you do not have enough room to completely cross the tracks. If you are on the tracks, you risk injury or death.'"

question: A curb painted red means:
options: "a: Loading zone.,b: The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c: No parking"
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Red: No stopping, standing, or parking.'"

question: When a school bus is stopped on the road ahead to load or unload children, you must:
options: "a: Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,b: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c: Change lanes"
note: "The DMV Handbook states that when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. This is to ensure the safety of children loading or unloading the bus."

question: You are approaching a green traffic light and traffic is blocking the intersection. What is the best thing to do?
options: "a: Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b: Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c: Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear."
note: "Even if you have a green light, do not start across the intersection if there are pedestrians or vehicles blocking your pathway.  It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red."

question: When passing, you should move back into the right lane when:
options: "a: You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c: You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, you should move back into the right lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. 'Signal and return to your original lane.'"

question: If a driver ahead of you has stopped at a crosswalk, you should
options: "a: Change lanes look carefully and pass,b: Tap your horn to let the driver know you are waiting,c: Stop then proceed when safe"
note: "You must stop for pedestrians at a crosswalk. 'Pedestrians always have the right-of-way. Here are some right-of-way rules at intersections:  - Green traffic signal light: Proceed with caution. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.'"

question: You are preparing to exit the interstate. When should you start reducing your speed?
options: "a: About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b: As you approach the deceleration lane.,c: Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'When in the proper lane, signal five seconds (approximately 400 feet) before you exit.' This indicates that you should start reducing your speed as you approach the deceleration lane, allowing ample time for a safe exit."

question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in a residential area is:
options: "a: 20 mph.,b: 25 mph.,c: 30 mph."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'The speed limit is 25 mph, unless otherwise posted.' in the section about business or residential districts."

question: You may drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle
options: "a: If the shoulder is wide enough to accommodate your vehicle,b: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left,c: Under no circumstances"
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.'"

question: You want to pass a vehicle on the road. You should
options: "a: Wait until you can see the entire vehicle in your rearview mirror before merging back into your lane,b: Use your horn to alert the other driver of your intention to pass,c: Pass only if there is enough space in the lane ahead of the vehicle,d: None of the above"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Unless you have enough space to return to your lane.' This means you should only pass if there is enough space in the lane ahead of the vehicle."

question: If you are repeatedly convicted for traffic violations
options: "a: DMV may impound your vehicle,b: Your driving privilege may be suspended by DMV,c: Both of the above"
note: "The DMV book states, ’DMV monitors your driver's record. As an adult or minor, if you get a traffic ticket and fail to appear (FTA) in court, DMV may suspend your driving privilege...As an adult, your license may be suspended if your driver's record shows one of the following point totals: 4 points in 12 months., 6 points in 24 months., 8 points in 36 months.'"

question: Large trucks turning onto a street with two lanes in each direction:
options: "a: May complete the turn in either of the two lanes.,b: Often have to use the left lane to complete the turn.,c: Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning."
note: The DMV Handbook states on page 42: 'When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. The longer the vehicle, the greater the difference in the length of the turning path. This is why large vehicles and truck drivers must often swing wide to complete a turn.'"

question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead. You should:
options: "a: Make eye contact with and then pass the pedestrian.,b: Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street."
note: "Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks. If there is a limit line before the crosswalk, stop at the limit line and allow pedestrians to cross the street."

question: You are driving and there are oncoming cars on your left and a row of parked cars on your right. You should steer:
options: "a: Closer to the oncoming cars than the parked cars.,b: Closer to the parked cars than the oncoming cars.,c: A middle course between the oncoming and parked cars."
note: "You should steer closer to the parked cars than the oncoming cars. 'If one danger is greater than the other, give more space to the most dangerous situation.' (Page 63)"

question: When it is legal to drive off the road to pass another vehicle?
options: "a: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b: It is not legal under any conditions.,c: If there are two or more one-way lanes."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.'"

question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road and there is no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?
options: "a: Straight ahead,b: Right,c: Left"
note: "When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right (toward the shoulder of the road). This will prevent your vehicle from rolling into oncoming traffic if the brakes fail.  'Turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail. Downhill: turn the wheels toward the curb.'"

question: In which of the following scenarios should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: "a: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c: When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 27 that when parked on a hill or sloping driveway, your wheels should be turned so the vehicle will not roll into the street. This is to prevent the vehicle from rolling if the brakes fail."

question: Which lights should be used if a driver is having trouble seeing other vehicles because of dust or smoke blowing across the roadway?
options: "a: Parking lights.,b: Emergency lights.,c: Headlights."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 11, 'Use your headlights: When conditions (such as clouds, dust, smoke, or fog) prevent you from seeing other vehicles.'"

question: In which lane should you end your turn when making a right turn?
options: "a: Any lane free of traffic.,b: The lane closest to the left edge of the road.,c: The lane closest to the right edge of the road."
note: "To make a right turn, you should end your turn in the lane closest to the right edge of the road. 'Do not swing wide into another lane of traffic.'"

question: If a motorist sees pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should the motorist do?
options: "a: Continue ahead. The motorist has the right-of-way.,b: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c: Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians."
note: "Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks. 'If there is a limit line before the crosswalk, stop at the limit line and allow pedestrians to cross the street.'"

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to make a right turn, you should:
options: "a: Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b: Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.,c: Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb."
note: "The DMV handbook states that when turning right, you should drive close to the right edge of the road.  It also states that when turning right from a one-way street onto a one-way street, you should start the turn in the far-right lane.  This means you should wait for the truck or bus to turn before you turn, rather than quickly turning before them or squeezing between them and the curb."

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
options: "a: Challenge them.,b: Get out of their way.,c: Speed up."
note: "The best course of action when encountering an aggressive driver is to get out of their way.  'If a tailgater is behind you. Maintain your course and speed. Then, when safe to do so, merge right to change into another lane and allow the tailgater to pass.'"

question: What should you do to make a right turn at an upcoming intersection?
options: "a: Merge into the bicycle lane before making the turn.,b: Wait until the bicycle lane ends then make the turn.,c: Make the turn from your current lane and do not enter the bicycle lane."
note: "To make a right turn, drive close to the right edge of the road. If a designated right turn lane is available, enter at the opening. You can drive in a bike lane within 200 feet from the turn. Check for bicyclists in your blind spots."

question: You must use your seat belt
options: "a: Unless you are riding in a vehicle built before 1978,b: Unless you are riding in a limousine,c: If the vehicle is equipped with seatbelts"
note: "The DMV handbook states 'You and your passengers must wear seat belts. You can get a ticket if you do not.'"

question: If your car becomes disabled while on the highway, you should:
options: "a: Stop in the right lane.,b: Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway,c: Stop where you are."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'If your vehicle stops working on the freeway: 1. Safely pull over to the right shoulder. 2. Exit on the right side so you are away from traffic if you must get out of the vehicle.'"

question: Once in the roundabout, drivers travel
options: "a: In a counter-clockwise direction,b: In a clockwise direction,c: In both directions"
note: "In a roundabout, traffic travels in one direction around a central island.  'Travel in a counter-clockwise direction. Do not stop or pass.'"

question: Driving so slowly as to interfere with normal or reasonable flow of traffic, except when necessary for safety, is
options: "a: A violation of the law,b: The right of any driver,c: Legal but not advisable"
note: "The DMV Handbook states: 'You must drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. At the same time, you should not block normal and reasonable traffic flow by driving too slowly. If you drive faster or slower than the speed limit, you may be cited.'"

question: When being followed by a tailgater, which of the following will help you avoid being hit from behind?
options: "a: Merging into another lane,b: Decreasing your following distance,c: Changing lanes frequently"
note: "To avoid a tailgater, you can merge into another lane when it is safe. 'Maintain your course and speed. Then, when safe to do so, merge right to change into another lane and allow the tailgater to pass.'"

question: If you parallel park facing downward on a hill:
options: "a: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,b: Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c: Keep your wheels straight."
note: "To park on a hill headed downhill, turn your front wheels into the curb or right toward the side of the road."

question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:
options: "a: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b: Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,c: Keep your wheels facing straight."
note: "As quoted in the DMV handbook: 'Headed either uphill or downhill when there is no curb: Turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail. Downhill: turn the wheels toward the curb.'"

question: When approaching an intersection that is controlled by a flashing red traffic signal, you must:
options: "a: Come to a complete stop,b: Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c: Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red."
note: "A flashing red traffic signal light means STOP. After stopping, you may go when it is safe."

question: Driving under the influence of any medication which impairs your driving is permitted:
options: "a: Under no circumstances.,b: If you don't feel drowsy.,c: If it is prescribed by a physician."
note: "It is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.  'The law does not see a difference between illegal drugs and medications you get from a doctor or pharmacy. They can all affect your ability to drive safely and react to what you see and hear.' (Page 72)"

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing in the middle of the street instead of in a crosswalk, you:
options: "a: Must stop for them.,b: Do not have to stop for them.,c: Should honk your horn at them."
note: "Even though they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.  'When there is a pedestrian crossing a roadway with or without a crosswalk, you **must** use caution, reduce your speed, or stop to allow the pedestrian to safely finish crossing.'"

question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if:
options: "a: You first come to a complete stop.,b: You wait until the light changes.,c: You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear."
note: "A green arrow means GO in the direction the arrow is pointing. The green arrow allows you to make a protected turn. Oncoming vehicles are stopped by a red traffic signal light. "

question: Various traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are the color:
options: "a: Red.,b: Orange.,c: Yellow."
note: "Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are typically orange. The DMV Handbook states:'Highway Construction and Maintenance Signs'. The signs shown in the image have black lettering and symbols on an orange background."

question: A safety zone is a specially marked area for passengers to get on or off buses or trolleys. You may not drive through a safety zone:
options: "a: Only when a bus or trolley is present.,b: Only when a bus or trolley is unloading passengers.,c: At any time or for any reason."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'Safety zones are spaces set aside for pedestrians waiting for buses, streetcars, and trolleys. Safety zones are marked by raised buttons or markers on a road. Do not drive through a safety zone under any condition.'"

question: When you prepare to make a left turn from a one-way road into a one-way road, you must
options: "a: Move into the left lane or to the left side of a single lane,b: Move into the right lane or to the right side of a single lane,c: Move into the right lane or to the left side of a single lane"
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'To turn left: Drive close to the center divider or into the left turn lane.' On a one-way street, you should be driving in the far left lane, so to turn left you should remain in that lane."

question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:
options: "a: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,b: Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.,c: Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking."
note: "You should always slow down before entering a curve, especially one that is downhill. 'Slow down as you approach intersections and curves. For sharp curves, slow down as you approach and move through.'"

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing in the middle of the street instead of in a crosswalk, you:
options: "a: Must stop for them.,b: Do not have to stop for them.,c: Should honk your horn at them."
note: "Even though they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.  'When there is a pedestrian crossing a roadway with or without a crosswalk, you **must** use caution, reduce your speed, or stop to allow the pedestrian to safely finish crossing.'"

question: To make a right turn onto a two-way street from a two-way street, start in the right-hand lane and end in
options: "a: Any lane that is available,b: The left lane,c: The lane closest to the curb"
note: "According to page 20, 'To make a right turn: Drive close to the right edge of the road... Complete your turn in the right lane. Do not turn wide into another lane.'"

question: Which of the following roadways freeze first when wet?
options: "a: Bridges and overpasses,b: Intersections,c: Tunnels"
note: "Bridges and overpasses tend to freeze before the rest of the road because they can have icy spots."

question: When following a motorcycle, drivers must remember that motorcycles can ____________ than other vehicles.
options: "a: Accelerate much faster,b: Stop much more quickly,c: Stop much more slowly"
note: "According to the DMV handbook on page 44, 'Allow a safe three-second following distance. This space will help you avoid hitting a motorcyclist if they brake suddenly or fall.'"

question: It is against the law to enter an intersection when:
options: "a: You can't get all the way across before the light turns red.,b: The light is flashing yellow and you didn't stop first.,c: The light is yellow and you cannot stop safely."
note: "According to the DMV handbook on page 34, 'Do not enter the intersection if you cannot get completely across before the traffic signal light turns red.'"

question: In which lane should you end your turn when making a right turn?
options: "a: Any lane free of traffic.,b: The lane closest to the left edge of the road.,c: The lane closest to the right edge of the road."
note: "To make a right turn, you should end your turn in the lane closest to the right edge of the road. 'Do not swing wide into another lane of traffic.'"

question: If you are feeling fatigued while driving, you should:
options: "a: Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.,b: Increase the volume of your radio.,c: Find a safe parking area to take a short nap."
note: "Fatigue and drowsiness can affect your vision and increase reaction time to hazards. 'Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.'  is the only option that directly addresses the issue of fatigue."

question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?
options: "a: A school crossing,b: A No Passing Zone,c: Yield"
note: "Pennant-shaped signs are no-passing zone signs. They are yellow with black lettering and are placed on the left side of two-way roads to warn drivers that passing is not safe in that area."

question: If you are driving and the rear end of your car starts skidding to the left, you should:
options: "a: Steer to the right.,b: Steer to the left.,c: Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral."
note: "To get out of a skid, you should steer in the direction of the skid. 'If you start to skid, follow these steps: 1. Slowly remove your foot from the accelerator. 2. Do not use the brakes. 3. Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid. 4. Try to get a wheel on dry pavement.'"

question: To avoid glare from the headlights of an approaching car:
options: "a: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b: Stay focused on the centerline on the road.,c: Flash your high beams."
note: "To avoid glare from the headlights of an approaching car, the DMV handbook states on page 59, 'Do not look directly into the oncoming headlights...Look toward the right edge of your lane...Do not react to the other driver by keeping your high-beam headlights on.'"

question: If traffic light is red, but a police officer or fire fighter on duty tells you to go ahead, you should
options: "a: Wait for the green light,b: Do as he or she tells you,c: Report him or her to police"
note: "Obey any direction, order, or signal given by a law enforcement officer, or firefighter. Follow their orders even if they conflict with existing signs, signals, or laws."

question: When driving on a multi-lane street with two-way traffic, you should:
options: "a: Drive alongside the other vehicles so the drivers can see you.,b: You should drive ahead of or behind the other vehicles.,c: It is safest to drive in the lane next to the center line."
note: "The DMV handbook states that you should drive ahead or behind the other vehicles to avoid collisions"

question: Which of the following increases your chances of being in a collision?
options: "a: Looking over your shoulder while making lane changes,b: Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles,c: Adjusting your rearview mirror before you start driving"
note: "Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles increases the risk of collision.  'Stay in one lane as much as possible. Do not weave in and out of traffic. Last minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.'"

question: If you become angry or upset, you should
options: "a: Go for a drive to forget your problems,b: 'Cool off' before driving,c: Control your emotions while driving"
note: "The DMV Handbook emphasizes the importance of controlling your emotions while driving, stating: 'If you become angry or upset, you should 'cool off' before driving.'"

question: When you want to change lanes, you should never:
options: "a: Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c: Check for other drivers moving into the same lane."
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Once you start moving through an intersection, keep going. If you start to make a turn, follow through.' (page 14) It is not safe to change lanes within an intersection as other vehicles may be approaching or already in the intersection."

question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:
options: "a: Buckle your safety belt.,b: Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c: Both of the above."
note: "The DMV handbook states that drivers should 'buckle up' and make sure that their 'passengers must wear seat belts.'"

question: BAC is
options: "a: The acronym for Beer Accumulation,b: The number of ounces of alcohol in your blood,c: The percentage of alcohol in your blood"
note: "The DMV handbook defines BAC as 'Your BAC is the amount of alcohol in your blood.'"

question: A driver should:
options: "a: Stare directly in front of their car.,b: Only focus on the middle of the road.,c: Watch beside"
note: "To drive safely, you need to know what is around you. 'To drive safely, you need to know what is around you.' DMV handbook pg. 57."

question: Left sign or the lane and sign should be used to warn of the reduction in the number of traffic lanes in the direction of travel on a multi lane highway. When parking uphill on a 2 way street with no curb, your front wheels should be
options: "a: Turn to the left toward the street,b: Turn to the right away from the street,c: Parallel with the pavement,d: Turn the wheels toward the curb"
note: "To prevent rolling downhill when parked on a hill with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right away from the street. 'Headed uphill: Turn your front wheels away from the curb (left - towards the center of the road) and let your vehicle roll back a few inches. The wheel should gently touch the curb. '"

question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if:
options: "a: You first come to a complete stop.,b: You wait until the light changes.,c: You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear."
note: "A green arrow means GO in the direction the arrow is pointing. The green arrow allows you to make a protected turn. Oncoming vehicles are stopped by a red traffic signal light. "

question: You enter a designated turn lane to make a left turn at an upcoming intersection. There is oncoming traffic. You should:
options: "a: Move to the left of the center lane.,b: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c: Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn."
note: "Before making any turns, it is crucial to signal your intention to other drivers. The DMV handbook states, 'Start signaling 100 feet before the turn.'"

question: Which of these statements is true about drinking alcohol and driving?
options: "a: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking,b: If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit,c: Alcohol affects judgement"
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Almost everyone feels negative effects of alcohol, even at levels lower than the legal limit.' This means that even if you're under the legal BAC limit, alcohol can still affect your judgment and make you an unsafe driver."

question: Which of the following statements about blind spots is true?
options: "a: They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c: Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors."
note: "The DMV handbook states that large vehicles and truck drivers have a better view in front of them and bigger mirrors, but they also have large blind spots, also called No Zones.  'In these areas, your vehicle can disappear from a large vehicle or truck driver's view. If you cannot see the truck's side mirrors, the truck driver cannot see you.'"

question: When a hazard is seen ahead, reaction distance
options: "a: Equals total stopping distance minus perception distance,b: Is how far a vehicle will continue to travel in ideal conditions before the driver hits the brakes,c: Is the sum of perception distance and braking distance"
note: "The reaction distance is the distance your vehicle will travel while you perceive the hazard and begin to react. It is the sum of the perception distance and the braking distance.  'To give yourself time to react, avoid last minute moves and hazards, always keep your eyes moving and scan the road at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.'"

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates that:
options: "a: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b: Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line."
note: "A broken yellow line indicates you may pass if the broken line is next to your driving lane. Only pass when it is safe. "

question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:
options: "a: Only if you are involved in a collision.,b: If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c: Only if you are stopped and cited."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 29, 'The driver of a stopped vehicle must produce a driver's license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration when stopped by law enforcement.' This implies that proof of insurance is required during a traffic stop, not just when involved in a collision."

question: Dim your headlights for oncoming vehicles or when you are within 300 feet of a vehicle:
options: "a: That you are approaching from behind.,b: Approaching you from behind.,c: That you have already passed."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 11, 'Dim your high-beam headlights to low beams within 500 feet of a vehicle coming toward you or within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.'"

question: The traffic light is green and you want to drive straight through an intersection. If a car is already in the intersection and is making a turn, you must
options: "a: Enter the intersection and then stop,b: Drive through the intersection. You have the right-of-way,c: Let that car complete its turn before you enter the intersection"
note: "Even if you have a green light, you must still yield to vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection. 'You should still stop for any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian in the intersection. Only proceed if you have enough space without creating a danger to any oncoming vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian.' "

question: How can you prevent fatigue on a long trip?
options: "a: Get enough sleep,b: Plan to drive long trips with a companion,c: All of the above"
note: "Page 9 of the DMV handbook states 'Fatigue and Drowsiness - Can affect your vision and increase reaction time to hazards.'"

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
options: "a: Challenge them.,b: Get out of their way.,c: Speed up."
note: "The best course of action when encountering an aggressive driver is to get out of their way.  'If a tailgater is behind you. Maintain your course and speed. Then, when safe to do so, merge right to change into another lane and allow the tailgater to pass.'"

question: How many days do you have to report to DMV the sale or transfer of your vehicle?
options: "a: 5 days,b: 10 days,c: 20 days"
note: "According to page 79, 'When you sell a vehicle, you must notify DMV within five days by completing a Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability at dmv.ca.gov/nrl.'"

question: What can you do to reduce road rage?
options: "a: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b: Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c: Use your horn frequently."
note: "Signaling your intention when changing lanes helps prevent other drivers from getting frustrated and reduces the chance of road rage. The DMV Handbook states that 'You should signal: At least 100 feet before you turn. Before every lane change.'"

question: You may drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle
options: "a: If the shoulder is wide enough to accommodate your vehicle,b: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left,c: Under no circumstances"
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.'"

question: When coming to a corner where there is a stop sign, you must first stop
options: "a: After crossing the crosswalk,b: Out far enough to see cross traffic,c: In back of the crosswalk"
note: "According to page 35, 'Make a full stop before entering the crosswalk or at the limit line. If there is no limit line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.'"

question: What should you do when there is a school bus ahead that starts flashing yellow warning lights?
options: "a: Slow down and prepare to stop.,b: Stop immediately and remain stopped.,c: Cautiously pass the school bus on the left."
note: "When a school bus flashes yellow lights, you must slow down and prepare to stop. 'Some school buses flash yellow lights when preparing to stop to let children off the bus. The yellow flashing lights warn you to slow down and prepare to stop.'"

question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line marking:
options: "a: You cannot cross the line to pass.,b: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,c: You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane."
note: "A broken white line indicates that you may cross the line to pass or change lanes."

question: It is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) that is ____ or higher.
options: "a: 0.08% -- Eight-hundredths of one percent,b: 0.10% -- One-tenth of one percent,c: 0.05% -- Five-hundredths of one percent"
note: "The correct answer is 0.08%.  This information can be found on page 73 of the DMV handbook. The DMV handbook states, 'It is illegal for you to drive if you have a BAC of: 0.08% or higher if you are over 21 years old.'"

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn:
options: "a: They may use the left lane.,b: They may cut through all lanes.,c: They may wait on the side of the road."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Bicyclists may… make left and right turns in the same way drivers do, using hand signals and turn lanes.'"

question: Blue traffic signs offer information on:
options: "a: Motorist services.,b: Construction and maintenance.,c: Mileage information"
note: "According to the DMV handbook on page 36, 'White Rectangular Sign' communicates many important rules you must obey."

question: Carpool lanes are marked with a diamond symbol. To use these lanes during the special hours shown on the signs you must
options: "a: Be driving a van or bus,b: Drive at the speed limit or have your lights on,c: Have the minimum number of passengers shown on the signs."
note: "Carpool lanes are marked with a diamond symbol and the words 'Carpool Lane'. 'To use an HOV lane, one of these must apply: You have a certain number of people in your vehicle. There will be signs at the on-ramp or along the road to tell you the minimum number of people. Road signs also list the hours when the HOV rules apply.'"

question: Make room for cars that are entering the freeway by:
options: "a: Slowing down.,b: Merging into a different lane.,c: Maintaining your speed and position."
note: "According to page 22, 'Make space for vehicles entering freeways, even if you have the right-of-way.'"

question: The first thing that alcohol effects is:
options: "a: Vision.,b: Judgment.,c: Balance."
note: "The DMV handbook states that alcohol can 'affect your ability to drive safely and react to what you see and hear.'"

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: "a: Reduce your speed.,b: Traffic light ahead.,c: Do not pass."
note: "A single solid yellow line marks the center of a road with two-way traffic. Do not pass a vehicle in front of you if there is only one lane of traffic going your direction and a solid yellow line on your side of the road."

question: Is it legal to use your horn in residential areas?
options: "a: Yes as long as you use it during the day,b: It is only legal if you live in the residential area,c: No it is not legal to use the horn in residential areas unless it is an emergency"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 10: 'Use your vehicle's horn to let other drivers know you are there or warn others of a hazard. Use your horn to: - Avoid collisions. - Alert oncoming traffic on narrow mountain roads where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead.'"

question: Which child would require a child passenger restraint system?
options: "a: A 9-year-old who is 4 feet 10 inches tall,b: A 10-year-old who is 5 feet 3 inches tall,c: A 7-year-old who is 4 feet 8 inches tall"
note: "According to The DMV handbook, children under 8 years old, or who are less than 4 feet 9 inches tall, must be secured in a child passenger restraint system in a rear seat. Option C is the only option that meets this criteria."

question: It is illegal to leave a child age six or younger unattended in a vehicle on a hot day:
options: "a: Even if they are secured in a child passenger restraint system.,b: If they are supervised by a person twelve years of age or older.,c: Only if the key is in the ignition."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'It is illegal to leave a child who is six years old or younger unattended in a vehicle...' and 'A child may be left under the supervision of a person who is at least 12 years old.'"

question: At a stop sign there is no stop line or crosswalk. You must stop
options: "a: Before you enter the intersection,b: After you enter the intersection if you have a clear view of traffic on the intersecting roadway,c: At the next crosswalk"
note: "According to page 35 of the DMV handbook, 'Make a full stop before entering the crosswalk or at the limit line. If there is no limit line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Check traffic in all directions before proceeding.'"

question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:
options: "a: Low beams.,b: High beams.,c: Fog lights only."
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'When it is raining, use your low-beam headlights.'"

question: Which of these vehicles must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: "a: Tank trucks with hazardous materials placards.,b: Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat trailer.,c: Sport utility vehicles carrying four or more persons."
note: "According to page 50, 'Vehicles with these signs must stop before crossing railroad tracks.'"

question: You can help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away from your vehicle by:
options: "a: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b: Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c: Maintaining a steady speed."
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Maintaining a steady speed' helps create space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead."

question: You should signal continuously while turning because it:
options: "a: Is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b: Lets other drivers know what your intentions are.,c: Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn."
note: "The DMV handbook states that you should signal when you turn because 'Always signal when you turn, change lanes, slow down, or stop. You can signal using your vehicle's signal lights or using hand-and-arm positions.'"

question: Water on the road can cause a vehicle to hydroplane. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: "a: 45 miles per hour.,b: 35 miles per hour.,c: 40 miles per hour."
note: "Hydroplaning occurs when driving in wet or rainy conditions.  Hydroplaning is when a vehicle rides on water because the tires lose all contact with the road. A slight change of direction, applying the brakes, or a gust of wind could throw the vehicle into a skid.  To avoid hydroplaning: Drive slowly. Steer around standing water, if possible. Slow down if you hear sloshing sounds from the tires. Slow down when changing lanes or direction."

question: You may drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle
options: "a: If the shoulder is wide enough to accommodate your vehicle,b: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left,c: Under no circumstances"
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, 'Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.'"

question: Which child requires a child restraint system?
options: "a: A six-year old who is 4 feet 10 inches tall,b: A seven-year old who is 4 feet 7 inches tall,c: An eight-year old who is 4 feet 9 inches tall"
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'Children who are under 8 years old, or who are less than 4 feet 9 inches tall: Secure in a child passenger restraint system in a rear seat.'"

question: When parking on a hill on a two-way street with no curb, you should:
options: "a: Turn your front wheels to the left away from the side of the road.,b: Park at a slight angle with rear wheels closer to the road's edge.,c: Turn your front wheels to the right toward the side of the road."
note: "To prevent your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail, you should turn your front wheels to the right, toward the side of the road.  'Turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail. Downhill: turn the wheels toward the curb.' "

question: If you come to a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights, you should:
options: "a: Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.,b: Come to a complete stop well behind the gates,c: Slow down and drive around the gates."
note: "When the crossing devices or a person warns you a train is coming, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest track."

question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:
options: "a: Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route to your destination.,b: Proceed to the next exit,c: Back up on the road or shoulder."
note: "According to the DMV Handbook, page 23,  'If you miss your exit, continue around until you return to your exit.'"

question: You should allow an extra cushion of space:
options: "a: When following a station wagon.,b: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c: When following a small passenger car."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Following other vehicles at a safe distance gives you enough time to react if another driver makes a mistake.'  This indicates that you should allow extra space when following a driver who may have a reduced field of vision or other issues that could impair their driving."

question: Alcohol is:
options: "a: A stimulant.,b: An antihistamine.,c: A depressant."
note: "Alcohol is a depressant. 'It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.'"

question: If an oncoming vehicle has started to turn left in front of you
options: "a: Maintain your speed and take your right of way,b: Honk your horn to warn the driver and maintain your speed,c: Slow or stop to prevent a collision"
note: "When turning left, do not assume that an oncoming vehicle with its right turn signal on is turning before it reaches you. The driver may have their signal on by mistake or plan to turn just beyond you. Wait for the vehicle to start its turn before beginning the left turn."

question: You must make a financial responsibility report after an accident when damage to one of the vehicles is over $750
options: "a: Only if you are not insured,b: Only if it was your fault,c: No matter who was at fault"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 77 that you must report the accident to DMV within 10 days if 'The collision caused more than $1,000 in damage to property.'"

question: Which of the following is true about driving in bad weather?
options: "a: You should always drive at the speed limit,b: Increase your following distance,c: Use cruise control to maintain speed,d: Drive with your windows down"
note: "The DMV handbook recommends increasing following distance in bad weather.  'Increase your following distance.'"

question: It is legal to drive with an alcoholic beverage container that has been opened only if the container is:
options: "a: Under the front seat.,b: In the glove department.,c: In the trunk."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, 'If you are carrying any alcohol, cannabis in your vehicle, the container must be sealed and unopened. If it is open, you must keep the container in the trunk or place where passengers do not sit.'"

question: Tailgating
options: "a: Is a defensive driving technique,b: Cannot result in a traffic citation,c: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry"
note: "Tailgating is following too closely, which can 'frustrate other drivers and make them angry.'  The DMV handbook states that it is important to leave a safe following distance. "

question: You drive defensively when you:
options: "a: Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b: Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c: Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards."
note: "Defensive driving is described as being aware of your surroundings, and the DMV handbook states that 'To drive safely, you need to know what is around you.'"

question: If you drive 55 mph in a 55 mph zone, you can be given a speeding ticket:
options: "a: Under no circumstances because it is always legal.,b: If the road or weather conditions require a slower speed.,c: Only if you are approaching a sharp curve in the road."
note: "The DMV Handbook states, 'In California, you may never drive faster than is safe for the current road conditions. This is known as the Basic Speed Law.'"

question: You should turn on your headlights:
options: "a: One half hour after sunset.,b: When stopped at a railroad crossing.,c: When parked at a school."
note: "The DMV Handbook states, 'Use your headlights: Beginning 30 minutes after sunset. Until 30 minutes before sunrise.'"

question: You should turn on your hazard lights when
options: "a: Driving in heavy rain or fog,b: Your car has broken down on the side of the road,c: You are double parked"
note: "The DMV handbook states 'If you need to stop because of vehicle trouble: - Turn on your emergency flashers. If your vehicle does not have emergency flashers, use your turn signals.'"

question: If there is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:
options: "a: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b: Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing."
note: "Pedestrians always have the right-of-way, even in unmarked crosswalks. 'Before entering an intersection, look left, right, and ahead to check for vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Be prepared to slow down and stop if necessary. Pedestrians always have the right-of-way.'"

question: If you are convicted of driving with an excessive blood alcohol concentration (BAC), you may be sentenced to serve:
options: "a: Up to six months in jail.,b: Up to 12 months in jail.,c: No jail time"
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 74 that you may be sentenced to up to six months in jail if convicted of a DUI. 'If you are convicted of a DUI, DMV will suspend or revoke your driving privilege for one year.'"

question: At dawn or dusk and in rain or snow, it can be hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn:
options: "a: Up the instrumental panel lights.,b: On your parking lights.,c: On your headlights."
note: "The DMV handbook states 'Use your headlights: When it is too dark to see from 1,000 feet away, Beginning 30 minutes after sunset, Until 30 minutes before sunrise, In adverse weather. If you need to use your windshield wipers due to fog, rain, or snow, you must turn on your low-beam headlights.'"

question: When planning to pass another vehicle, you should:
options: "a: Not count on other drivers to make room for you.,b: Assume the driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.,c: Assume the driver will maintain a constant speed."
note: "The DMV handbook states that 'Never assume that other drivers will give you the right-of-way.'"

question: Which of the following increases your chances of having a collision?
options: "a: Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles,b: Adjusting your rearview mirror before you start driving,c: Looking over your shoulder while making lane changes"
note: "Continuously changing lanes to pass other vehicles is dangerous as it can lead to collisions.  'Stay in one lane as much as possible. Do not weave in and out of traffic. Last minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.'"

question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas:
options: "a: Have a red background with green writing.,b: Have an orange background with black writing.,c: Have a yellow background with blue writing."
note: "The DMV handbook states on Page 36 that 'Diamond-Shaped Sign Warns you of specific road conditions and dangers ahead.'"

question: With a Class C driver's license, a person may drive
options: "a: a light rail train,b: car or van or pickup truck,c: semi truck"
note: "On page 7, The DMV handbook states 'Most people need a noncommercial Class C driver's license.'  On page 1, it states 'For information on vehicles covered by a Class C, visit dmv.ca.gov/dl.'"

question: California's basic speed law' says, in addition to obeying the maximum speed limit, drivers must keep in mind
options: "a: The posted speed limit,b: Synchronized stop lights,c: Road traffic and weather conditions"
note: "The DMV book on page 67 states: 'In California, you may never drive faster than is safe for the current road conditions. This is known as the Basic Speed Law.'"

question: When parking your vehicle parallel to the curb on a level street:
options: "a: Your front wheels must be turned toward the street.,b: Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.,c: One of your rear wheels must touch the curb."
note: "According to the DMV handbook, when parallel parking your vehicle, 'Your vehicle should now be parallel and within 18 inches of the curb.'"

question: If a road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:
options: "a: No different than normal.,b: Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c: Closer to the car ahead than normal."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Drive more slowly than you would on a dry road. Adjust your speed for different conditions: ... Wet road: Reduce your speed by 5 to 10 mph.'"

question: Which of the following substances can affect the ability to drive?
options: "a: Tranquilizers,b: Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c: All of the above."
note: "The DMV Handbook clearly states 'It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.' It also says, 'No matter what age you are, it is illegal to drive after... Taking any drug that affects your ability to drive. This includes prescriptions or over-the-counter medications.'"

question: An orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle always means:
options: "a: The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b: Slow-moving vehicle.,c: Shoulder work ahead."
note: "The DMV handbook states on page 45 that 'Some slow-moving vehicles have an orange and red triangle on their back, such as road maintenance vehicles which usually travel at 25 mph or less.'"

question: Having a driver license is a:
options: "a: Right,b: Privilege,c: Requirement."
note: "The DMV Handbook states that a California driver's license 'allows you to drive on public roads.'"

question: Carpool lanes are marked with a diamond symbol. To use these lanes during the special hours shown on the signs you must
options: "a: Be driving a van or bus,b: Drive at the speed limit or have your lights on,c: Have the minimum number of passengers shown on the signs."
note: "Carpool lanes are marked with a diamond symbol and the words 'Carpool Lane'. 'To use an HOV lane, one of these must apply: You have a certain number of people in your vehicle. There will be signs at the on-ramp or along the road to tell you the minimum number of people. Road signs also list the hours when the HOV rules apply.'"

question: When driving at night with no other vehicles ahead, a driver should use
options: "a: High beam lights,b: Low-beam lights,c: Parking lights"
note: "When driving at night with no other vehicles ahead, a driver should use high-beam headlights. 'When driving at night, use your high-beam headlights on open country roads or dark city streets.'"

question: Blocking an intersection during "rush hour" traffic is not permitted:
options: "a: Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.,b: Under any circumstances,c: Unless you have the right-of-way or a green light."
note: "It is against the law to stop or block an intersection where there is not enough space to completely cross before the traffic signal light turns red.  This is found on page 39."

question: You are driving on a one-way street. You may only turn left onto another one-way street if:
options: "a: You increase your speed before the turn.,b: Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c: Traffic on the street moves to the left."
note: "You may turn left against a red light when you are turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists who have a green light. Look both ways and turn when it is safe."

question: Which of these statements is true about changing lanes?
options: "a: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.,b: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,c: Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots."
note: "Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors, check traffic behind and beside you, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure the lane is clear."

question: What does a traffic signal with a yellow left arrow indicate?
options: "a: Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b: The protected left turn is about to end.,c: Both of the above."
note: "A yellow arrow means the protected turning time is ending. The signal will change soon. If you cannot stop safely or you are already in the intersection, cautiously complete your turn. Pay attention to the next signal. It could be a: - Green or red traffic signal light. - Red arrow."

question: Never make a U-turn:
options: "a: In residential districts.,b: At or on a railroad crossing.,c: Where there isn't a ‘No U-turn’ sign posted."
note: "The DMV handbook states, 'Never make a U-turn: ... At or on a railroad crossing.'"

question: At an intersection with stop signs at all four (or more) corners, when two cars arrive at the same time you must yield the right-of-way to the driver
options: "a: On your right,b: On your left,c: Signaling a turn"
note: "The DMV handbook states: 'If a vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist gets to the intersection at the same time as you, give the right-of-way to the vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist on your right.'"

question: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a thin film of water instead of on the surface of the road. To prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather, you should:
options: "a: Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b: Decrease your speed.,c: Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain."
note: "To avoid hydroplaning, the DMV handbook states: 'Drive slowly.' 'Slow down if you hear sloshing sounds from the tires.'  'Slow down when changing lanes or direction.'  (Page 61)"

question: When driving on an interstate, to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right, the best thing to do is to:
options: "a: Change lanes to the left.,b: Slow down.,c: Maintain your speed and position."
note: "To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps, you should change lanes to the left if it is safe to do so.  The DMV handbook states, 'Make space for vehicles entering freeways, even if you have the right-of-way. Be ready for rapid changes and watch for signals from other drivers.'"

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:
options: "a: Passing is permitted from the left.,b: Passing is permitted from the right.,c: Passing is not permitted from either direction."
note: "Double solid yellow lines indicate a lane barrier and passing is not permitted from either direction. 'Do not pass over double solid yellow lines.'"
